Let me now think carefully about each mechanic's design.

**The core constraint set (locked invariants):**

- Invariant 6: Cost equals the natural roll. → Any movement test is a Core Test paid at natural roll from its resource domain (PE for Body skills, MP for Mind skills). Movement itself (non-test) is free/bundled (DEC-095). The mechanics here shouldn't create "movement points" spent from a pool — Invariant 17.
- Invariant 17: No competing primary resource/progression economy. → Movement Speed is a *derived statistic* (DEC-004), not a spendable pool. Movement distance per turn = effective MS (DEC-133(3)). A "consuming mechanic" consumes *distance*, not a resource pool. Contested-movement consumption (DEC-133.A R2) is open: whether the mover's MS is reduced, the opponent's, or none. Any candidate that spends MS as a pool must be flagged — e.g., "spend 2 MS to Disengage" creates a spendable pool out of a derived stat; that's arguably fine (not a *currency*/progression economy; it's the same thing movement already is — a per-turn budget). Hmm. Actually DEC-133 states "Movement Distance per combat turn = effective Movement Speed; 1 MS = 1 hex per turn". This is already a per-turn budget — every combatant can move up to effective MS hexes per turn as a free side activity. "Consumption" in DEC-133.A R2 means: when a contested movement (e.g., a Chase opposed test) occurs, does the success/failure consume any of the mover's or opponent's movement distance? This is a design fork, not an invariant violation, as long as it doesn't create a persistent pool that carries between turns (that would be Invariant 17 territory — a stored resource). I should note this carefully: per-turn budget consumption is fine; anything persisting across turns or accumulating is a new pool → Invariant 17 risk.

- Invariant 18: modules must call the Core Test Transaction, not replace it. → All resists/contests use S-1 (DEC-013) with full Cost/Overflow/XP/Recovery. No free "reaction rolls" for movement unless they're full Core Tests or full S-1 contests.

- DEC-007.A: Overflow immutability — contest outcomes must never modify Overflow. Movement effects can't change HP-damage outcomes.

- DEC-023.A policy: no damage-over-time; no natural-roll modification; one Effect per win (DEC-024); Position-tier Effects list.
- DEC-107: Effect Tier = Skill-Tier of causing skill; winner selects any Effect their Skill Tier and Skill permit; Quality = tie-break + success precondition. Magnitude Z = −Y for records.
- DEC-030: fail-and-fall-back for Tag/Location-gated Effects — Position-tier effects are NOT Tag/Location-gated (they're Tier-gated by Skill-Tier? Actually the gating for Position tier: DEC-023.A's Position tier is a "gated tier" that "unlocks automatically when its dependency locks". The dependency here is the G5 movement model, which is now locked (DEC-133). So Position-tier effects are now unlocked/selectable. DEC-099's ≥10 Quality gating was superseded by DEC-107 — so there's no numeric Quality threshold; the winner may select any Effect their Skill Tier permits. Skill-Tier ≥ 2 gate is only for Location-index-requiring effects (DEC-041); Position-tier effects like Forced Movement don't necessarily need a Location Index... but wait — DEC-041 item (1)/(6)? DEC-142 says none of the location-referencing Effect language is touched. Position-tier Effects per DEC-023.A have no Tag + Location gating listed (only Equipment and Disarm/Break Hold do). So the Position-tier Effects (Forced Movement; Knock Prone; Seize/Deny Ground; Pin/Hold Position; Open/Close Lane) are selectable on a winning S-1 contest, subject only to the winner's Skill-Tier permitting the Effect? Hmm — actually per DEC-107, "the winner may select any Effect their Skill Tier and Skill permit". For a Tier-1 position effect — is there a minimum Skill Tier? DEC-023.A says the gated tiers "unlock automatically when its dependency locks". What's the Skill-Tier requirement? DEC-107 says Effect Tier = Skill-Tier of the causing skill. So a Position Effect's record Tier Y = causing skill's Skill-Tier. The effect is "selectable" presumably at any Skill-Tier since Position-tier effects aren't gated by DEC-041's ≥2 (that's for Location Index). I'll note that as a recommendation: Position-tier Effects selectable at winning Quality ≥ 1 (success precondition), record Tier = causing Skill-Tier, Magnitude Z = −Y, per DEC-107/115. Given there's ambiguity in the minimum tier unlock, I'll flag as open question (does a Tier-1 character with no ≥2 skills unlock Position effects? DEC-023.A says gated tiers unlock when dependency locks — the dependency is the movement model, now locked; so yes, unlocked for all; but I'll present this as interpretation with recommendation).

- DEC-095: movement free/bundled; one substantive action per turn; S-1 exchange per turn.
- DEC-122/123/124/125/131: movement-denial conditions; Grappled contested break-hold.
- DEC-138: uniform −Y overlay for movement penalties.
- DEC-132/132.A/132.B: reactions — movement-trigger category exists, tag-gated, resolved as full S-1 opposed contest, uncapped, independent of Active Defense. **Important**: Disengage and ZoC are natural movement-trigger reaction hooks, but the tags must be content-authored; the framework level should reference the movement-trigger category without inventing specific tags? Actually DEC-132.B R3(2) registered the `reaction:` namespace and one-tag-per-category. The movement-trigger category is a defined taxonomy category. So the consuming-mechanics framework may invoke: "a movement-trigger reaction (DEC-132.A R1/DEC-132.B R3) fires on position/band changes" — as a framework-level reference, not authoring a specific tag vocabulary (that stays DEC-077.A content-authoring). But wait, DEC-132.B R3 adopted one tag per category at content level: the exact tag for movement-trigger would need Tiwa's content ruling. The framework can note the hook exists.

**Now the seven mechanics. Let me design each.**

---

**M1. Disengage**

What it is: a mover in Engagement range of an opponent who wants to leave Engagement (move into Short or further) without being automatically followed/struck. In many TTRPGs (D&D 5e: Disengage action; GURPS: retreat/withdraw rules; PF2e: Step, Tumble Through, Withdrawal) — leaving melee is risky.

Constraints: movement is free/bundled (DEC-095) — so Disengage can't be a "substantive action" swap without amending DEC-095 (which is Locked/Canonical). Options:
- (A) Disengage is resolved as an S-1 opposed contest at the moment the mover declares movement out of Engagement (mover's appropriate skill — e.g., an Acrobatics/Evasion lineage — vs. the opponent's reactive skill or the trigger-fired movement-trigger reaction). Success → mover moves up to effective MS free; failure → movement out of Engagement restricted (options: no movement, half movement, or move but trigger an attack-of-opportunity-style exchange).
- (B) Free-form: leaving Engagement without opposition is always allowed; the opponent gets a movement-trigger reaction (tag-gated, DEC-132) to contest it — i.e., Disengage is the *baseline* rule "leaving Engagement is permitted; an opposing movement-trigger reaction may contest it". This makes Disengage a zero-mechanic default with an optional contest when tags exist.
- (C) Asymmetric-cost model: disengage costs extra movement (e.g., backpedaling costs 2 hexes per hex moved while in Engagement? No—that reopens DEC-133's unit definition, and adds per-hex costs that contradict "movement is free"). Rejected risk: creates a movement-point economy.

The "consumption" question (DEC-133.A R2): what does a failed Disengage contest consume? Candidates: (i) nothing beyond normal Cost (the contest's natural-roll cost); (ii) the mover's remaining movement distance for the turn; (iii) the opponent's. This is a genuine fork — present alternatives.

Also interplay with Grappled: DEC-131 already covers Grappled move-away (contested Break Hold, success = stepwise removal, failure = locked, no relocation). So Disengage must not overlap: Disengage governs leaving Engagement when the mover is NOT Grappled/Restrained; Grappled uses DEC-124/131 machinery. Boundary rule needed.

**M2. Zone of Control (ZoC)**

What it is: an entity with a melee presence threatens the space around it — the Engagement band. In band terms, the natural ZoC is: any tracked entity attempting to move *from Engagement into Short* (leave) or *from Short into Engagement* (approach into contact) changes the band relative to that entity. The simplest Tiwas-native implementation: ZoC is **not a separate mechanic at all** — it's the definition of the Engagement band (DEC-133(2): "entities are immediately engaged; melee interaction is spatially direct"). Entering/leaving Engagement is governed by Disengage (leaving) and by the standard move-then-engage procedure (entering). ZoC as a *modifier/denial* mechanic (e.g., movement through an opponent's Engagement zone without engaging) is where a rule is needed:
- (A) Pass-through rule: moving *through* an opponent's Engagement band (from Short to Short across their hex, or Medium→Short→Medium past them) requires either (i) their consent (narratively: they let you pass) or (ii) a contested movement test (Tumble/Acrobatics vs their relevant skill) — fail = blocked (mover stops at the boundary) or, harshly, forced stop + the opponent may apply a free exchange.
- (B) ZoC is purely tag/content: creatures with a `combat:hold-the-line`-style authored ability deny pass-through; default = pass-through free. (Keeps framework minimal.)
- (C) ZoC = automatic reaction trigger only (no denial): passing through Engaged space triggers a movement-trigger reaction opportunity (DEC-132) if the opponent has the tag; otherwise pass-through is free.

Recommendation: A-with-B-content-hook or C; present alternatives. Careful: "forced stop" must not be a free attack (one Effect per win DEC-024; no free exchanges outside contests; DEC-101 no counter-Effect). Any "attack of opportunity" would be a full S-1 exchange — flag as open question whether Tiwas wants opportunity attacks at all, and note DEC-132's movement-trigger reaction category as the existing vehicle (requiring an authored tag? Content-authoring). Hmm, actually the reaction framework requires a reaction-granting tag; the exact trigger menu is content-authoring. So the framework can say: pass-through denial resolves via a movement-trigger reaction (S-1 contest) only when the denying entity has an authored reaction-granting tag; otherwise pass-through is permitted. That's Option C — zero framework-level denial, which is elegant and respects DEC-132.

**M3. Chase**

What it is: pursuit where both parties move (medium/far bands), resolved over time. Constraints: movement is per-turn, turn order per DEC-095 (Speed-based). Chase needs: (1) a resolution primitive (the "generic movement contest" M4!), (2) band dynamics (distance change per round), (3) consumption (does the chase consume the chaser's/runner's movement? — DEC-133.A R2).

Design: a Chase is a *sequence of S-1 opposed contests*? Or a single S-1 contest with sustained results? Options:
- (A) Per-round movement contest: each round of the chase, both parties make an S-1 opposed contest with an appropriate Movement-affiliated skill (e.g., Running/Quickness lineage); winner's Quality (margin) determines band change (content boundary per DEC-133.A R1... wait, band↔hex conversion boundaries are content-authoring DEC-077.A — so the Quality→band-change table is content, not framework). Chase ends when bands reach Engagement (caught) or the chaser concedes/breaks off (narrative or declared), or a threshold (target beyond Far → escape, via content table).
- (B) Margin-accumulation (Extended Test shape, DEC-067/068): chase is an Extended Test where each round's contest margin accumulates toward a target determined by... but Extended Test targets are GM discretion (DEC-070/074). This converts Chase into margin accumulation — viable, uses existing machinery, but adds target-selection complexity.
- (C) Single decisive contest: one S-1 contest resolves the chase; band change read off quality. Simpler but less Priority-1-realistic and interacts poorly with turn-by-turn movement.

Also: how do conditions/terrain apply? Conditions apply −Y overlays to the relevant stats (DEC-138). A chase is a natural place for the "effective Movement Speed" already being the contested stat. **Key fork**: contest on a *Skill* (Core Test) vs contest on raw **effective Movement Speed** (a derived stat, no roll — would that violate Invariant 18? A speed-vs-speed comparison isn't a Core Test — no roll — could be resolved deterministically or by... hmm. If no roll, it's not a Core Test; but Invariant 18 prohibits *replacing* the Core Test with another engine, not prohibiting deterministic comparisons. Yet a Chase with no rolls would violate the identity "every meaningful attempt uses the common resolution engine" (§1 Core identity) and would produce no Cost/XP/Overflow — an XP hole. So the primary lane is a full Core Test/S-1 contest; Movement Speed can serve as a *secondary discriminator* or the contest's Quality scale, e.g., "Hybrid/Margin where the tracked quantity is the delta of effective Movement Speeds"... careful. Simple recommendation: Chase = S-1 opposed contest using a movement-relevant skill per participant; effective Movement Speed used as (i) the deterministic tie/range-limit: a character cannot close a gap larger than their effective MS in one round — i.e., band movement is capped by effective MS; and (ii) possibly as the Quality formula's primary identity (Hybrid Committed?). Present as alternatives.

Consumption fork (DEC-133.A R2) for chase: does the chase consume movement for the rest of the turn? Recommend: chase movement IS the turn's movement (the runner's movement budget is spent running); following characters spend their movement to pursue. If a chaser has movement left after closing the gap, they may act normally? Edge case; note as open.

**M4. Generic movement contests**

What it is: the universal primitive for any opposed movement resolution (Stealth vs Perception while moving? Shove-back? Bull rush? Blocking? Forced entry past a defender? Grapple-adjacent? Tumble past — M2; Disengage — M1; Chase — M3). DEC-133.A R3 lists it as its own open item — i.e., a *generic* rule for "movement contest" distinct from the named ones. Deliverable: define the generic form — any opposed movement test is an S-1 opposed contest (DEC-013) on an appropriate movement skill; the natural-roll costs apply; Outcome reads off the winner; the *spatial payload* (band/hex/position change) is governed by the specific mechanic (M1–M3) or by content (DEC-077.A) where the situation isn't one of the named ones. Also the consumption question gets its generic answer here: DEC-133.A R2's open question — define what a generic contested movement consumes. Options: (i) nothing extra — contest cost only; (ii) the loser's movement; (iii) both parties'; (iv) winner's margin read as hexes consumed. Present the fork honestly.

The generic contest must also specify which Skills are legal (content-authoring? or framework default: any skill the GM deems applicable per DEC-106 §2 multiple-applicable-skills economy; recommend GM fiat + declared intent DEC-025).

**M5. Forced Movement magnitude**

What it is: the Position-tier Effect "Forced Movement" (DEC-023.A) — e.g., a shove, knockback, push, pull. Magnitude missing: how far does the target move? Options:
- (A) Winner's Margin read as hexes of forced movement: target moves `min(Margin, ...)` hexes away? But Margin = Skill − Roll can be large (up to 99+). Content clamp per band (DE-077.A).
- (B) Record-scaled: the Effect record carries `Tier Y / Magnitude Z` with Z = −Y (DEC-115 R2) — but "Forced Movement magnitude" is a *distance*, and Z = −Y is a penalty-magnitude convention for Conditions. For a Position effect, distance Y could be "the target moves Y hexes" — Tier-scaled: **the Effect's Tier = causing Skill-Tier (DEC-107); the target is moved Y hexes** (flat, e.g., 1 hex per Tier, or floor(MS/2) etc. — content). Recommendation: distance = Y hexes (Tier-scaled, mirroring Z = −Y in magnitude), content-clamped to band boundaries, direction away from the effector (or per declared vector), subject to forced-movement interaction rules (collision? push into hazards? into other entities? over edge?) — these are content questions (DEC-077.A), but the framework should define whether forced movement provokes reactions/ZoC and whether it overrides movement-denial conditions (it's not "movement" by the mover, it's external displacement — so Restrained/Grappled/Prone total-locks (DEC-122) and DEC-131 grapple relocation prohibition... careful: DEC-131 says relocation of either combatant is NOT an outcome of a move-away attempt — but forced movement is a different source (an Effect), so it's not preempted by DEC-131? DEC-131 (3) "Relocate both branch DROPPED: relocation of either combatant is not an outcome of a move-away attempt" — this is about the grapple-move-away attempt specifically. Forced Movement as an Effect from a winning contest is a separate channel; flag as interaction question: Can Forced Movement move a Grappled character? Recommend: yes (it's externally imposed), but no relocation in the Grappled move-away sense; the grapple persists relative to position? This is a genuine open interaction → question list.
- (C) Contest-delta: like Inflict Injury contest-delta (DEC-104), magnitude = winner's Margin − defender's AD margin (if defensed)... but defense of Forced Movement: Active Defense applies to any auto-applied Effect (DEC-050). So Forced Movement magnitude could mirror DEC-103/104: contest-delta, mitigated by Active Defense, surviving record native. Hmm — DEC-103 is for Wound/Condition Effects; DEC-104 for HP. For Position-tier effects there's no ruled mitigation formula. Recommend: Forced Movement magnitude = the Effect's own Tier Y hexes (per B) — with DEC-103-style step-1/step-2 mitigation available since DEC-050 allows AD vs any Effect... but the mitigation machinery (Tier/Margin) was ruled for Effect application generally in DEC-103 — "Applies to Effects only, never HP". So Forced Movement (an Effect) can be mitigated via DEC-103 machinery: Mag −(shred), Mag −= defender's margin; floor 0 → Tier −1, etc. But then "Tier Y / Magnitude Z, Z = −Y" with magnitude-as-distance gets weird: DEC-115 defines Z = −Y as the penalty magnitude. For Forced Movement, is the record a Condition-type record with Z = −Y (penalty to the target's position?) or is "magnitude" measured in hexes? Genuine fork:
  - (i) Record-native: `Position Tier-Y Forced Movement` with Magnitude Z = −Y; the *mechanical payload* is Y hexes of displacement (Tier-scaled); mitigation via DEC-103 reduces Y (Tier-mutation via AD).
  - (ii) Contest-delta hexes: displacement = winner's margin (clamped), independent of record Tier; the record's Tier gates healing/removal only... but Forced Movement is instant (displacement happens immediately), so a persistent record isn't needed unless knockback causes Prone (separate Knock Prone effect) or the target is 'pinned at the wall'.
  
  Recommend (i) with instant application: record Y determines hexes moved; the record persists only as long as needed (identical to how Wounds are instant but recorded). Flag alternatives.

**M6. Pin/Hold Position resolution**

What it is: Position-tier Effect "Pin / Hold Position" — you win a contest and the target cannot leave their position (held in place, being pinned down). This is a *movement-denial* effect — must join the DEC-122/123/124/131 movement-denial framework consistently:
- D&D: grapple/pin; GURPS: grappling/pinning.
- Tiwas constraints: "no action denial" — DEC-123 "never total": a Pinned character may still declare actions; they auto-fail? No — hmm, DEC-123's "never total" applies to Stunned/Incapacitated/Restrained action-declaration. Prone/Grappled/Restrained are distinct identities (DEC-023.A(3)). Pin/Hold = new mechanical identity? Or maps to Grappled/Restrained? Options:
  - (A) Pin/Hold Position = a **Condition-tier-equivalent placement**: the Effect imposes the existing `Restrained` or `Grappled` Condition record (DEC-079 alpha vocabulary), i.e., Pin/Hold is a *route into the Condition system*, not a new record. Resolution = the normal contested Break-Hold machinery (DEC-124/131) to escape. This maximizes reuse and honors "complete answer" closures (DEC-082.A R2: DEC-122/123/131 are the complete answer for movement-denial × Movement Speed...). But careful: DEC-082.A R2 said "no further interaction mechanics ruled" for movement-denial × Movement Speed — adding a *new* denial Condition would need to slot in. Mapping Pin/Hold onto Restrained (global) which already has the self-referential-Y total-lock zeroing movement (DEC-122) — but then "never total" action-declaration (DEC-123) applies — fine.
  - (B) Pin/Hold Position as a stand-alone Condition-tier record `Tier-Y Pinned/Held Position`, with its own overlay −Y (via DEC-138 uniform formula) — new Condition, content-authoring per DEC-077.A? But Condition vocabulary is alpha-locked (DEC-079); adding a Condition needs an amendment.
  - (C) Pin/Hold = the Seize/Deny Ground effect applied to the *mover* (i.e., pins the person to the ground = Knock Prone + Seize/Deny combination) — no.
  Recommend (A): resolve Pin/Hold Position as imposing the existing `Restrained` (or, where limb-grappled, `Grappled`) Condition per the S-3 Effect → Condition route (DEC-023.A Condition tier naming shows Pin/Hold is Position-tier, but the *payload* can be an existing Condition — this respects DEC-113-style tier assignment? Hmm, actually careful: In DEC-023.A, Pin/Hold Position is listed under Position Tier, not Condition Tier. The "tier" is the menu tier, payload can differ. There's precedent: DEC-060 Sunder listed Condition-tier and DEC-079 C8 made it Condition+Tag. So an Effect at one tier routing to Condition machinery is precedented (Sunder).
  Resolution open question: what does the pinned target's escape require? Recommend DEC-124/131 Break Hold / Break Free contested machinery (identical to Grappled escape), and note that DEC-124's contest rule governs "moving away from" — for Pin the denial should also block changing bands. Also the Duration: holds until escape attempt succeeds or the pinner releases/incapacitated — mirror DEC-079 Grappled "ends by Break Hold, grappler incapacity, or forced separation."

**M7. Seize/Deny Ground resolution**

What it is: Position-tier Effect "Seize / Deny Ground" — winner takes the position / prevents the loser from occupying ground (e.g., pushing someone back a band, planting on a point, denying a lane — neighbor Open/Close Lane). Resolution needed:
- (A) Ground-seizing = a *band/hex relocation + occupancy claim*: on a win, the victor advances into the contested position's band (or holds it) and the loser retreats one band (Short→Medium etc.) — i.e., Seize/Deny Ground is resolved as a **forced band change for the loser + protected occupancy for the winner** (the winner's position can't be displaced by the loser's normal movement without a new contest — same as DEC-124's no-relocation from a *failed* move-away: the loser may not cross back into the seized band without winning a new contest).
- (B) Lane-specific: Open/Close Lane is the directional form (seize a corridor); Seize/Deny Ground is area form. Both read off the same resolution: on success the declared ground/lane changes ownership band; on failure nothing changes (fail-and-fall-back? No — DEC-030's fail-and-fall-back applies to Tag/Location-gated Effects only; for Position-tier: on a winning contest, the selected Position Effect applies; there's no "partial" — binary, consistent with DEC-030's rejection of graded outcomes).
- Magnitude: distance of the loser's displacement = the record Tier Y (consistent with M5's Tier-scaled hexes) or content (DEC-077.A)? Recommend same Tier-scaled convention as Forced Movement for consistency.

**Cross-cutting "consumption" (DEC-133.A R2) fork** — this is the one explicitly-open decision in the register: what does a contested movement consume?
- Option 1: Nothing beyond the contest's Core Test cost (each participant pays their natural roll; movement isn't additionally consumed).
- Option 2: The mover's movement budget (if the mover's contest fails, their movement for the turn is spent/partially spent).
- Option 3: Both parties' movement.
- Option 4: Quality-based consumption (loser's Quality as hexes forfeited — the winner chases them down: loser's remaining distance reduced; effectively merges with the band-change payload).
Present all four with consequences; do NOT decide.

**Where do these mechanics sit as Effects?** DEC-023.A Position tier: Forced Movement; Knock Prone; Seize/Deny Ground; Pin/Hold Position; Open/Close Lane. Note DEC-133.A R3 names Disengage, ZoC, Chase, generic movement contests as *consuming mechanics* — they're frameworks around movement, not necessarily S-3 Effect menu entries. Only Forced Movement magnitude, Pin/Hold Position resolution, Seize/Deny Ground resolution are Position-tier Effects needing magnitude/resolution. Disengage/ZoC/Chase/generic contests are procedural mechanics (movement procedures), which is why DEC-133.A R3 calls them "consuming mechanics ... as Position-tier Effects under DEC-023.A" — hmm, actually the register says "Seven consuming mechanics ... all remain open as Position-tier Effects under DEC-023.A — not preempted by this amendment." Reading: Disengage, ZoC, Chase, generic movement contests are *consuming mechanics* (they consume movement), placed under the Position tier umbrella (they interact with the Position-tier). I'll treat them as Position-tier-adjacent procedural mechanics rather than menu Effects, and note the reading.

Now, deliverables format: For each mechanic: (a) rules text (candidate implementation — I'll write cleanly, with bracketed evidence-class tags and [OQ] markers), (b) evidence class for every claim, (c) open questions / alternative framings.

I need to be disciplined: every claim tagged with evidence class: mechanical fact / empirical finding / designer ruling / recommendation. I'll use inline tags like **[mechanical fact: ...]** or a per-paragraph evidence ledger. Given (b) "evidence class for every claim", inline tagging is cleanest: `[EC: mechanical fact — Canonical §6]`.

Let me also do the Invariant 6/17 audit explicitly for each mechanic (the task demands the constraints "must satisfy the Core Invariants ... (esp. Invariant 6 Cost = natural roll, Invariant 17 no competing resource pools) and DEC-133.A R3").

Where to store: `proposals/` — since these are candidate implementations (Proposed / WIP per status vocabulary). File name following repo conventions: `tiwas-movement-consuming-mechanics-candidate-implementations-2026-09-19.md`.

Wait — I must check: does the repo have a canonical/ folder? The glob for proposals showed only one file in proposals/, plus the sources/... Let me check the repo structure for canonical/ and investigations/ conventions, and whether there's a proposals README. Let me check the README and directory structure.

## Where to look

| If you want... | Go to |
|---|---|
| The current locked Tiwas ruleset | `canonical/rules/` |
| How this documentation is governed (authority, status, provenance) | `governance/` |
| What's implemented/being sequenced, and why it isn't a rules source | `roadmap/` |
| Non-canonical candidate mechanics, open design questions | `proposals/` |
| The evidentiary/analytical work behind those proposals | `investigations/` |
| The original, unmodified source material | `sources/` |
| Historical/superseded material | `archive/` (currently empty — see `archive/README.md`) |
| How this consolidation was performed, and what remains for human review | `_consolidation/` |

## Quick orientation

- **Only `canonical/rules/` is canonical game-mechanics source.** Everything else is either non-canonical design material, implementation/process guidance, or governance-of-the-documentation-itself.
- If you're an LLM picking up this project cold, read `governance/authority.md` and `governance/status-model.md` before making any claim about what is or isn't a rule.
- Several items described in exhaustive detail in `proposals/` and `investigations/` (e.g., the S-2 attack-side invocation policy, the S-2 non-attack deferral) are **real designer rulings but not Canonical rules** — see `_consolidation/decision-register.md` for the distinction.

I have all the context I need. Now let me draft the proposal document. The task asks: "design candidate implementations for the seven consuming mechanics named in DEC-133.A R3... For each mechanic give: (a) rules text, (b) evidence class for every claim, (c) op..." — the task was truncated at "(c) op" — clearly "(c) open questions / alternative framings" per my drafter duties ("Produce alternative framings when the section is genuinely open; do not silently collapse open questions into one option").

I'll write the document to `proposals/tiwas-movement-consuming-mechanics-candidate-implementations-2026-09-19.md`.

Key structural elements:
1. Governance preamble verbatim (as given in my system prompt).
2. Provenance frontmatter.
3. Spec card (reconstructed from task brief + DEC-133.A R3, since no spec-card directory exists yet — flag that it is self-declared for this draft).
4. Constraint lock-set summary (evidence-classed).
5. Shared substrate (band model, movement consumption fork, Effect-selection machinery).
6. Seven mechanics, each: (a) rules text candidates, (b) evidence classes, (c) open questions + alternative framings.
7. Invariant 6 / 17 audit table per mechanic.
8. Designer question list (no silent resolution).
9. File storage note: proposals/, non-canonical.

Author identity: The system prompt says: "You are powered by the model named big-pickle. The exact model ID is opencode/big-pickle." Existing repo convention for this model's outputs: `author_llm: {name: "opencode", version: "big-pickle"}` (see orchestration plan frontmatter). I'll use that. created_date 2026-09-19. status: Non-canonical advisory.

Now let me carefully craft the content. I want to be thorough but well-organized. Length: This is a big design doc; substantial but not bloated. I'll aim for a rigorous, dense document.

Let me think about the design details again, per mechanic, with the constraint analysis:

### Locked set relevant to all seven (the "constraint ledger")
- Invariants 1–16, 18 (Canonical §16) — esp. 6 (Cost = natural roll), 17 (no competing resource/progression economy), 18 (build on Core Test Transaction; no replacement engine). Mechanical fact.
- DEC-004 Movement Speed formula. Mechanical fact (Canonical/Locked).
- DEC-006 9-step Core Test. Mechanical fact.
- DEC-007.A Overflow immutability (cited in DEC-130 bound; also DEC-007). Designer ruling (non-canonical ruling but operative). Actually DEC-007.A — let me note it's the Overflow immutability ruling. It's a designer ruling recorded in the register.
- DEC-013 S-1 opposed contest. Canonical/Locked. Mechanical fact.
- DEC-023.A Position-tier alpha content + no-DoT + no-ADV/DIS + Invariant 6/17 lock + one Effect per win. Designer ruling.
- DEC-024/024.A one Effect per win; second effect via separate contested roll (DEC-026 different Advanced Skill; DEC-049 independent AD; DEC-030 fallback). Designer rulings.
- DEC-025 Effect identity = declared intent, no Skill-side gating. Designer ruling.
- DEC-030 fail-and-fall-back only for Tag+Location-gated Effects (Disarm/Break Hold, Equipment Damage, Armor Bypass); binary outcomes; no graded/residual Effects. Designer ruling.
- DEC-031 superseded gating clause; Quality = tie-break + success precondition (≥1 floor) per DEC-107. Designer ruling.
- DEC-041 Skill-Tier ≥ 2 production gate for Location Index-affecting effects. Designer ruling.
- DEC-095 turn structure; movement free/bundled; one substantive action = one S-1 exchange; AD nested. Canonical/Locked (ruled).
- DEC-106 creature/NPC multi-attack + GM fiat action selection. Designer ruling.
- DEC-107 Effect Tier = causing Skill-Tier; winner selects any Effect their Skill Tier and Skill permit; lesser tier = Player choice + GM Fiat; Quality = tie-break/success-precondition. Designer ruling.
- DEC-115/117 unified record schema `Type / Tier Y / Magnitude Z / [Location X]`; Z = −Y. Designer rulings.
- DEC-122 self-referential-Y total lock (Stunned/Incapacitated/Restrained/Grappled/Prone movement zeroing), provisional. Designer ruling.
- DEC-123 "never total" action-declaration. Designer ruling.
- DEC-124 Grappled move-away = contested Break Hold; relocate deferred → DEC-131. Designer ruling.
- DEC-125 Prone crawl floor-of-1. Designer ruling.
- DEC-131 Grappled fail-vs-relocate: Pure Break — fail = locked, no relocation; success = stepwise Heal-Effect-System removal; relocate-both dropped. Designer ruling.
- DEC-132/132.A/132.B reactions: movement-trigger category; tag-gated; full S-1 contest; uncapped; one tag per category; `reaction:` namespace; trigger menus content-authoring. Designer rulings.
- DEC-133 G5 Hybrid: bands + hex; MS = hexes/turn; band↔hex content; DEC-095 reference; contested-movement consumption open. Designer ruling.
- DEC-133.A R1–R3: band↔hex content-authoring (R1); contested-movement consumption open (R2); seven consuming mechanics open as Position-tier Effects (R3). Designer ruling.
- DEC-138 G1: uniform Z = −Y overlay; no table; DEC-077.A content exceptions; DEC-122 provisional unaffected. Designer ruling.
- DEC-130 GM Fiat bounded universality. Designer ruling.
- DEC-077.A content-authoring. Designer ruling (amendment).
- DEC-079 alpha Condition vocabulary (Grappled/Restrained/Prone defined). Designer ruling.
- DEC-082.A R2: DEC-122/123/131 "complete answer" for movement-denial × Movement Speed; co-occurring denial Conditions not separately ruled. Designer ruling.
- G3 open (duration) — not blocking (G1/G3 brief §2.3 — empirical/analytical observation that none of the seven requires real seconds). Note as recommendation-level dependency.

### Shared substrate decisions I must NOT silently make (open forks):
1. Contested-movement consumption (DEC-133.A R2) — four options; do not pick.
2. Which Skill is legal for movement contests — DEC-106 §2 multiple-applicable-skills + GM fiat + DEC-025 declared intent; default guidance = any movement-relevant skill the GM accepts; creature defaults content-authored (DEC-098 Brawling default precedent is for defense only — do not extend).
3. Whether Position-tier Effects require a minimum Skill-Tier — DEC-023.A "gated tiers unlock when dependency locks"; dependency (movement model) now locked → interpretation: unlocked; flag as open question asking Tiwa to confirm no additional Skill-Tier gate beyond DEC-107's Tier assignment (Tier Y = causing Skill-Tier).
4. Whether movement-trigger reactions are required to implement ZoC/Disengage or only optionally available (content-authoring per DEC-077.A).
5. Interaction of Forced Movement with DEC-122 total-lock conditions (can a Restrained character be shoved?) and DEC-131's no-relocation-in-grapple (is forced relocation of a grappled pair allowed?).

### Draft rules text per mechanic

I'll write "Candidate implementation" text with a "preferred recommendation" where I present one as recommended but ALWAYS flag the fork, per duties. Actually my duty: "Produce alternative framings when the section is genuinely open; do not silently collapse open questions into one option." So each mechanic section: candidate rule text (primary), alternative framings, open questions. I can recommend but must not silently decide.

**M1 — Disengage.**
Candidate (recommended): When a combatant declares movement that will take them out of an opponent's Engagement band *during that turn's movement*, the opponent may resolve a movement-trigger reaction (DEC-132/132.A R1/132.B R3) contesting the departure **only if they possess an authored reaction-granting Tag in the movement-trigger category** (content-authoring per DEC-077.A; no framework-level Tag is authored here). The contest is a full S-1 opposed contest (DEC-013); mover uses an evasion/agility-lineage skill of their choice (declared intent, DEC-025; GM acceptance per DEC-106 §2), opponent uses a skill of equal standing. Outcomes:
- Mover wins: departure occurs; the mover spends their normal movement to reach the target band; consumption per the generic consumption ruling (M4/OQ-CONS).
- Opponent wins (or no Tag → no contest): departure is still resolved as normal movement unless denied by another rule (Grappled → DEC-124/131; Restrained → DEC-122/123). I.e., the *default* is: leaving Engagement is freely permitted; the contest exists only to create consequences on failure (which consequences = the consumption fork, OQ-CONS) — not to forbid movement outright (DEC-123 "never total" discipline: movement-denial Conditions deny via overlay, not by contest veto, except the ruled Grappled case DEC-124/131).
- Alternative A (Veto model): opponent win → mover may not leave Engagement this turn (movement spent or retained per consumption rule). Rejected-by-default on DEC-123-spirit, but presented.
- Alternative B (Cost-shift model): disengaging from Engagement costs extra movement distance (e.g., double-cost hexes while inside an opponent's Engagement band) — flagged as creating a movement-budget modifier that DEC-133 defines as flat 1 hex = 1 MS; a per-hex surcharge is a content-level amendment to DEC-133(3), would need its own ruling; risk of drift into a movement-point economy (Invariant 17).
Also note attack-of-opportunity-style "free strike" is architecturally excluded (DEC-024 one Effect per win; DEC-101 no counter-Effect; any opportunistic strike would be its own full S-1 exchange = a reaction, tag-gated).

**M2 — Zone of Control.**
Two senses:
(1) ZoC-as-band-definition (mechanical fact from DEC-133(2)): Engagement band = zone where melee interaction is spatially direct. Any entity in Engagement with a combatant is within that combatant's influence. Recommended framework rule: entering an opponent's Engagement band does not require permission (movement into Engagement is normal movement); leaving it is governed by M1.
(2) ZoC-as-pass-through-denial: moving *through* an opponent's Engagement zone without engaging (e.g., Short→(through their hex)→Short on the far side, or crossing to reach an ally behind them). Candidates:
- Recommended (Reaction-gated): pass-through is permitted by default; the occupying combatant holding an authored movement-trigger Tag may contest the passage with a full S-1 opposed contest (same machinery as M1). Opponent win → the mover's path is blocked: the mover's movement ends at the near boundary of the Engagement band (they may stop, choose a different path, or attempt a new contest); consumption per OQ-CONS. Mover win → passage succeeds.
- Alternative (Denial-as-convention, D&D-style): ZoC denies pass-through *by default* for any combat-capable entity; only an S-1 win (mover) allows passage. More restrictive; higher tactical friction; needs a ruling on whether the default should be permissive or restrictive.
- Alternative (No ZoC mechanic): ZoC = nothing beyond bands; passing through Engaged space is always permitted; only reactions (M1/M2 machinery) can alter outcomes. Simplest; zero framework footprint; risks pass-through exploits in tactical playtests (empirical: the mirror-match playtest lacked positional asymmetry evidence — no empirical contrast available).
Also: ZoC-as-denial of movement *within* Engagement (maneuvering around an engaged opponent to flank) — content-authoring or generic contest (M4) — flag.

**M3 — Chase.**
Recommended framework: A Chase is a sequence of S-1 opposed movement contests, one per combat round, with three possible lane states: engaged (caught) / trailing at a band (gap) / escaped (beyond max closing range). Per-round resolution:
- Each participant rolls a full Core Test (S-1 form) on a movement-appropriate skill.
- Band-change payload: the winner's contest outcome moves the gap one band step per the content-authored band↔hex boundaries (DEC-133.A R1/DEC-077.A); i.e., the framework defines *that* band change happens, the exact hex↔band mapping stays content.
- Effective Movement Speed caps closing: a pursuer cannot close more hexes in a round than their effective MS (DEC-133(3)); equivalently in band terms, a gap larger than MS cannot be closed in one round (content boundary). This keeps Speed meaningful without a second engine.
- Distance accounting (consumption): both parties' chase movement counts as their normal movement for the round (they are both spending their movement to run); consumption abuse per OQ-CONS.
- Escape threshold: content (e.g., when the gap exceeds the pursuer's effective MS and a content boundary holds for N rounds, the target escapes) — DEC-077.A.
- Alternative A (Extended Test): Chase as a DEC-067/068 Extended Test with a GM-set completion target (DEC-070) and margin accumulation; does not require per-round contests; but changes the XP/time texture and removes turn-by-turn interplay (Priority 1 vs Priority 3 trade-off).
- Alternative B (Single decisive contest): one S-1 contest; Quality sets the band delta; no multi-round structure. Minimal; loses granular simulation (Priority 1).
- Alternative C (Speed-vs-Speed deterministic): compare effective Movement Speeds directly, no rolls → excluded as architecturally hostile: "every meaningful attempt uses the common resolution engine" (§1 identity is Canonical); deterministic resolution produces no Cost/Overflow/XP/Double material (Invariant 6/18 and progression economy harm) — present as excluded with reasoning (evidence class: architectural constraint + mechanical fact), noting exclusion reasoning is mine (recommendation) though the underlying constraints are mechanical fact.

**M4 — Generic movement contests.**
Recommended framework text: Any movement-conflict situation not covered by M1–M3, M5–M7 (e.g., shoving past a blocker, muscling through a crowd, holding a doorway, wading against a current, a creature blocking a corridor) resolves as a single S-1 opposed contest (DEC-013) using the skill each participant declares (DEC-025) accepted by the GM (DEC-106 §2); each participant's Core Test is full (cost/overflow/XP/doubles/recovery — DEC-006/007/009/012). The spatial/positional payload of the win is determined by the specific rule that governs the situation; where no specific rule exists, the payload is either (a) the interplay of the consumption ruling OQ-CONS + the band model, or (b) content-authoring (DEC-077.A). Two framing alternatives:
- A (Framework-minimal): generic contests exist only as the fallback resolution primitive; no additional magnitude machinery.
- B (Payload-standard): define a default payload — "winner's Quality adjusts the loser's position one band per content boundary; ties per DEC-013.4/13.5" — a convenience default that overtly defers the band↔hex mapping to content.
Also: third-party adjudication on mutual failure (S-8/DEC-043 pattern) referenced, but DEC-043 is non-canonical — I should mention it only as a cross-reference with status flag. Actually the register cites "S-8 DEC-043 non-canonical for third-party adjudication" in the adaptation report; DEC-043 in the register — I didn't verify its text; safer to cite the register line via the adaptation report as non-canonical reference, or skip. I'll reference it carefully as "the S-8 third-party adjudication pattern (advisory; see adaptation-report mapping)" — better: keep to DEC-013's repeat rule and note third-party adjudication is outside scope. Keep simple: mutual failure → repeat (DEC-013 §13.4); exact-quality tie → repeat (§13.5).

**M5 — Forced Movement magnitude.**
Recommended: The Position-tier Effect "Forced Movement" displaces the target Y hexes (or one band per content boundary) in a declared direction, where Y = the Effect's Tier = the causing Skill's Skill-Tier (DEC-107), recorded in the unified schema as `Tier-Y Forced Movement, Magnitude Z = −Y` (DEC-115 R2 form; magnitude is the penalty convention, the displacement is the payload). Active Defense may mitigate per DEC-050/DEC-103-style machinery (recommendation: apply DEC-103's step-1 shred + step-2 margin de-escalation to the displacement; survivor displacement = max(0, Y − shred − margin) hexes; AD failure → no mitigation per DEC-097). The target's path must not pass through occupied bands/entities/hazards without content adjudication (DEC-077.A): recommend default "the displacement stops at the first occupied entity or obstructed boundary" (no collateral knock-back chain by default; content may author knock-through, which could trigger new S-1 contests — flag: knock-through into another combatant would be an Effect on a third party, which one-Effect-per-win (DEC-024) doesn't forbid but would need explicit ruling).
Alternatives:
- (A) Record-Tier-scaled hexes (recommended, above).
- (B) Winner's-Margin hexes: displacement = winner's Quality (Margin), clamped by content (band boundaries). Distinct feel: Big-margin thunderclaps shove farther; but Quality is not currently a magnitude source for any Effect post-DEC-107 (it's tie-break + success precondition only) — introducing Quality-as-magnitude here would reopen DEC-107's settled role; flag as needing a deliberate ruling if chosen.
- (C) Contest-delta (DEC-104-style winner's margin − defender's margin) as hexes — mirrors HP channel; but again reads margin as magnitude.
- (D) Content-only: displacement magnitude not ruled at framework; every Forced Movement instance authors its own (violates "Forced Movement magnitude" being explicitly listed open in DEC-133.A R3 — the register wants a magnitude settled at framework or clearly delegated; so present the delegation option honestly but mark that it would leave the named open item unresolved-by-framework and is only acceptable if Tiwa says so).
Interactions: Forced Movement vs DEC-122 zeroed states (a Restrained/Stunned target being shoved: the overlay zeroes their own movement, not external displacement — recommend displacement still applies; flag as open). Forced Movement vs DEC-131 grapple no-relocation rule (see M7/flag); Forced Movement vs Prone (follow-on knock prone is a separate Effect "Knock Prone" — cannot be granted by the same win per DEC-024 — flag: pushing someone down uses one Effect; each win selects exactly one Position Effect).

**M6 — Pin/Hold Position resolution.**
Recommended: "Pin / Hold Position" resolves by imposing the existing `Restrained` Condition record (DEC-079 alpha vocabulary; DEC-115/117 record form `Tier-Y Restrained, Magnitude Z = −Y`, Location global or limb) on the target, created by the winning contest's Effect selection (Tier = causing Skill-Tier, DEC-107). Consequences: the existing Restrained machinery applies (movement total-lock via DEC-122 overlay zeroing; action-declaration still permitted but auto-fail per DEC-123 "never total"; escape = a contested Break Hold/Break Free attempt per the Grappled-escape pattern, DEC-124/131 machinery by analogy — the escape route is the same contested skill check; success stepwise-removes the record per the Heal Effect System shape DEC-121). Where the fiction is a limb-level grapple instead of a full body pin, use `Grappled` instead (Location limb or global) — the two Effects route to the two existing Conditions; distinct identities preserved per DEC-023.A(3).
Alternatives:
- (A) Route-to-existing-Condition (recommended; respects DEC-082.A R2's "DEC-122/123/131 complete answer" closure — a new denial Condition would break that closure).
- (B) New alpha Condition "Pinned/Held" authored via amendment to DEC-079 (heavier; new record, new duration rules; DEC-082.A R2 marks co-occurring denial Conditions as not separately ruled — creating a new one would need explicit amendment).
- (C) Pin as pure positional hold (no Condition record: the target simply may not change bands while the pinner holds; escape via generic movement contest M4) — lighter than a Condition; but "cannot change bands" is itself a movement denial which DEC-122's overlay machinery expresses via Restrained; a positional-only rule risks conflicting with the "complete answer" closure.
Open: duration — until a successful escape contest, the pinner releases, or the pinner is incapacitated (mirror DEC-079 Grappled removal routes); whether the pinner is themselves movement-restricted while pinning (recommend: yes — holding a pin consumes the pinner's position, i.e., the pinner also stays in Engagement; this is a positional commitment, content or framework? flag).

**M7 — Seize/Deny Ground resolution.**
Recommended: On a win, "Seize / Deny Ground" changes the *ownership* of the contested position: the victor occupies the declared ground (band/hex/feature) and the loser is displaced to the adjacent band away from it (displacement distance = per the M5 Tier-scaled convention, for consistency; or immediately adjacent band — content boundary). While the ground is seized, the loser may not re-enter or pass through it without winning a new contest (a generic movement contest M4 or a declared attempt); moving *through* is additionally covered by ZoC pass-through rules (M2) if the winner holds an authored tag, else by M4. "Deny" flips the payload: the victor declares ground the loser may not enter (a barrier claim); the loser attempting entry must win an M4 contest. Both are binary (DEC-030 discipline — no graded outcomes).
Alternatives:
- (A) Position-ownership (recommended).
- (B) Band-relocation-only (loser displaced one band; no persistent claim) — simpler, but loses the "seize" identity (the ground isn't held).
- (C) Lane-convention: fold Seize/Deny Ground into Open/Close Lane's machinery (Lane = directional seize); both read the same resolution (flag: Open/Close Lane is a separate Position Effect name in DEC-023.A; whether they share one resolution is content/consolidation question).
Open: interplay with DEC-131 (grappled pairs) — can Seize/Deny displace a grappled pair (as a pair) or is the grappled pair's position locked? Recommend: displacement of a grappled pair is not an outcome of an *attempt to move away* (DEC-131) but a third-party Effect is a different source — flag as open question.

### The master consumption fork (OQ-CONS) — presented, not decided:
- F1 No-additional-consumption: contested movement costs only the normal Core Test costs; no movement budget consumed beyond what the mover already declared.
- F2 Mover-spends: on a failed contest, the mover's remaining movement for the turn is consumed (partially or fully) even though they did not complete the move (movement spent attempting).
- F3 Both-spend: both parties' movement for the turn is consumed by the contest (they committed to the interaction).
- F4 Quality-transfer: the loser's Quality is read against the band model (loser loses position/movement equal to their Quality per content boundary) — merges consumption with payload.
Each has Invariant-17 consequences analysis: F2/F3 temporarily "absorb" the per-turn budget — the per-turn movement budget is not a stored currency (Invariant 17 concerns *persistent* pools: Skill Roll Pool temporary (Inv 9); movement vanishes at turn end) — so F2/F3 are compliant as long as consumption never persists across turns and never accrues. F4 reads Quality as magnitude → DEC-107-era caution (see M5 alt B).

Also: the seven mechanics' interplay with the *reaction* framework (DEC-132 family): all movement-changing events are natural movement-trigger candidates, but framework-level triggers menus are content (DEC-132(4)/132.A R1/132.B R3). The candidate rules reference the movement-trigger *category* without authoring tags.

### Invariant 6/17 audit table (per mechanic):
- Disengage: all rolls full Core Tests; no dice modification; no pools → pass.
- ZoC: same → pass.
- Chase: same → pass (unless deterministic speed-only variant → fails 18/identity; flagged).
- Generic contests: same → pass.
- Forced Movement magnitude: magnitude from record Tier (no new pool); AD mitigation reads DEC-103 machinery → pass; margin-as-magnitude alternative flagged for DEC-107 tension (not an invariant violation per se — Quality is still a read-only scalar — but a design-ruling tension).
- Pin/Hold: routes to existing Condition records → pass.
- Seize/Deny: positional, no pools → pass.
No mechanic introduces: stored points, per-scene counters, second XP channels, or parallel resolution engines. Each contested roll is a full Core Test with natural-roll cost (Invariant 6) paid from PE/MP (Canonical §7) with Overflow (DEC-007), XP (DEC-009), Double (DEC-012), Recovery (DEC-008) intact.

### Designer question list (do not resolve):
1. OQ-CONS master consumption fork F1–F4 (DEC-133.A R2).
2. Position-tier menu unlock: confirm no additional Skill-Tier gate beyond DEC-107 Tier assignment (interpretation of DEC-023.A "unlock when dependency locks").
3. ZoC default posture: permissive (reaction-gated) vs restrictive (default denial).
4. Opportunity-strike vehicle: confirm movement-trigger reactions (tag-gated, full S-1) are the only vehicle; no free strikes.
5. Forced Movement magnitude: Tier-scaled hexes vs margin-based vs content-delegated; and forced movement vs DEC-122-zeroed targets; forced movement of grappled pairs (DEC-131 interplay).
6. Pin/Hold: route-to-Restrained/Grappled vs new Condition vs positional-only.
7. Seize/Deny: ownership model vs relocation-only; Open/Close Lane consolidation.
8. Chase: sequence vs extended-test vs single contest; escape thresholds content.
9. Knock-through/knockback collision handling (content default vs framework).
10. Whether these seven should be promoted as one package or per-mechanic (process question — G1 gate).

Also flag the G3 note (not blocking; no real-time duration needed for any of the seven) — from the G1/G3 brief §2.3, an analytical observation (advisory).

Also there's the naming of this document: follow repo convention `tiwas-<topic>-<date>.md`: `tiwas-movement-consuming-mechanics-candidates-2026-09-19.md`.

Also I should include a "spec card" section per my duty: purpose, status, dependency chain, locked invariants, open questions. Since no spec-card exists in the repo (P0 backbone not yet run for this section), I'll mark it as "spec card as reconstructed from the task brief + DEC-133.A R3; self-declared for this draft; to be reconciled with the backbone when P0 runs."

One more check — DEC-097 (failed AD → mitigation 0): cited from DEC-103 summary. Good.

DEC-104: Inflict Injury contest-delta = winner's Margin − defender's Margin (per active-defense-effect-mitigation ruling file §5.7). Good.

DEC-105: melee-exchange algorithm — one S-1 contest per exchange; both roll; defense voluntary in live play, mandatory in playtests. Good.

Now, evidence-class tags: I'll use a compact inline notation `[EC: mechanical fact — Canonical §6 / DEC-006]`, `[EC: designer ruling — DEC-133.A R3]`, `[EC: empirical finding — mirror-match playtest 2026-09-11]`, `[EC: recommendation — this draft]`, `[EC: architectural constraint — Canonical Invariant 18]`. Per the status-model, evidence classes: mechanical fact, empirical finding, designer ruling, recommendation, architectural constraint. I'll use architectural constraint where apt.

Let me now also double-check one important calibrage: DEC-133.A R3 says the seven are open "as Position-tier Effects under DEC-023.A". DEC-023.A Position tier = Forced Movement; Knock Prone; Seize/Deny Ground; Pin/Hold Position; Open/Close Lane. Disengage, Zone of Control, Chase, generic movement contests are NOT among that list — so the register is saying these *consuming mechanics* (which consume movement) are open and sit within the Position-tier *umbrella* (i.e., the movement/position subsystem), not that they are S-3 menu entries. +> (e.g., an agility/evasion-lineage Skill per DEC-025 declared intent), defender
+> rolls their declared reactive Skill.
+>
+> - **Mover wins:** departure succeeds; the mover completes the declared
+>   movement (consumption per Fork C, §4.1).
+> - **Defender wins:** the mover's movement for this turn ends at the boundary
+>   of the Engagement band they attempted to leave; they may still perform
+>   non-movement actions (DEC-095), may attempt a new disengage (another S-1,
+>   another Core Test cost), or may abandon movement entirely. Movement is
+>   denied by position, never by action-veto (DEC-123).
+> - **No Tag, no reaction:** no contest; the departure is free normal movement
+>   unless movement is otherwise denied (Grappled → DEC-124/131 break-hold
+>   contest is required; Restrained/zeroed MS → normal movement is already 0).
+
+Rationale trace: reaction-scoped (Tag-gated) so the framework adds no universal
+"opportunity attack"; mover-equivocation of the outcome (positional denial, not
+action denial) obeys DEC-123; one full S-1 contest per attempt (DEC-006/013);
+consumption left open (Fork C). [EC: designer rulings above; recommendation — this shape] 
+
+### (b) Alternative framings (not collapsed)
+
+- **Option B — free leave + opponent option only (no contest on leave):**
+  leaving Engagement is always free movement; the only cost the opponent can
+  impose is a *separate* declared action (e.g., a Strike via their own
+  substantive action), not a reaction. Simpler, but makes disengage trivially
+  safe against melee — likely too weak a denial for ranged/pursuit play.
+  [EC: recommendation]
+- **Option C — movement-extra-cost model:** leaving Engagement costs +Y hexes
+  of Movement Distance. Risk: this amends DEC-133(3)'s flat "1 MS = 1 hex"
+  conversion per-hex — a per-path surcharge is a new movement arithmetic that
+  DEC-133.family did not settle and that drifts toward a movement-point
+  economy (Invariant 17 watch). Presented because "attack of opportunity →
+  extra movement cost" is a genre-common pattern; not recommended as a clean
+  fit for the locked movement frame. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-133(3) is flat 1:1; recommendation — flag; Invariant 17 caution]
+- **Option D — auto-fail stance:** a defender *always* contests a disengage
+  (no Tag needed). This converts disengage into a universal S-1 roll every

+## 6. M2 — Zone of Control (ZoC)
+
+### (a) Candidate rules text (Option Z1 — permissive default + gated pass-through denial)
+
+> **Zone of Control.** A combatant's ZoC is the hexes of their Engagement band
+> (DEC-133 band model; band↔hex content per DEC-133.A R1).
+>
+> - **Entering** another combatant's Engagement band is always permitted (normal
+>   movement) — no permission roll, no reaction by default.
+> - **Passing through** an occupied Engagement band (entering and leaving it in
+>   the same movement, with the intent to not stop inside it) may be contested
+>   by the occupying combatant **if and only if** they hold an authored
+>   movement-trigger Tag (same reaction machinery as Disengage, §5). On the
+>   occupier's win, the mover's movement ends at the near boundary of the
+>   contested band (positional denial, DEC-123-compliant) and the consumption
+>   fork (§4.1) applies; on the mover's win, passage succeeds.
+> - **No framework-level "no entry/no passage" law is created here.** Band
+>   denial is either (i) tag-gated reaction machinery (above) or (ii) the
+>   positional ownership effects of Seize/Deny Ground (§11). ZoC does not grant
+>   free strikes: inflicting harm is a separate Effect selection (DEC-024) or a
+>   declared action, never an automatic property of movement denial.
+> - **Movement within** another combatant's Engagement band (e.g., circling to
+>   flank) is a generic movement contest only when contested fiction demands it
+>   (§8); otherwise it is normal movement.
+
+Rationale: this is the minimal ZoC consistent with the locked frame — the
+framework defines the *band* as the zone, and denies *passage* only through the
+reaction machinery that the register already provides for movement triggers.
+It avoids both (i) automatic free attacks (DEC-024/DEC-101 counter-Effect
+prohibition) and (ii) a framework-level no-passage law that DEC-030/DEC-123 do
+not license. [EC: designer rulings — DEC-024/101/123/132; recommendation]
+
+### (b) Alternative framings
+
+- **Option Z2 — restrictive default (genre-standard):** passing through an
+  occupied Engagement band is *prohibited by default*; only a successful S-1
+  contest (mover) allows passage. This is the D&D-style ZoC. It creates a
+  universal denial law at the framework level — a heavier footprint than the
+  register's tag-gated reaction design and gives every defender a free
+  contest-denial without a Tag. Whether the designer wants this "sticky
+  engagement" texture is exactly the open fork (Q4). [EC: recommendation]
+- **Option Z3 — no framework ZoC at all:** ZoC = purely descriptive band
+  geometry; all denial is content-authored (terrain, specific creature rules,
+  Seize/Deny Ground Effects). Zero framework footprint; likely too weak for
+  melee-front protection in a tactical game (no empirical data either way).
+  [EC: recommendation; empirical finding — no playtest coverage of ZoC]
+- **Option Z4 — ZoC as movement-suppression aura:** entities inside your
+  Engagement band have their Effective Movement Speed reduced (−1 hex) while
+  inside. This is a +Y overlay on Z = −Y machinery (DEC-115/138) — seductive,
+  but it converts a *positional* rule into a *condition-like penalty* outside
+  the Condition record system (DEC-079 alpha vocabulary), which the movement-
+  denial closure (DEC-082.A R2) warns against. Presented, not recommended.
+  [EC: designer ruling — DEC-082.A R2, DEC-138; recommendation]
+
+### (c) Evidence classes & open questions
+
+- Mechanical facts: band model from DEC-133(2); reaction machinery DEC-132.
+- No empirical data (mirror-match playtest had no ZoC/pass-through scenario —
+  [EC: empirical finding]).
+- Open: permissive vs restrictive posture (Q4); whether entry-into-Engagement
+  should also be tag-gated (recommendation: no — entry is the defender-friendly
+  act; denial targets exit/passage); interplay with Seize/Deny Ground (§11).

+## 7. M3 — Chase
+
+### (a) Candidate rules text (Option K1 — sequential S-1 movement contests, band-driven)
+
+> **Chase.** When one party (the FLEEER) moves with the declared intent to
+> break off and the other (the PURSUER) declares pursuit as that turn's
+> substantive action (DEC-095 — one S-1 exchange per turn), resolve a Chase as
+> a sequence of S-1 opposed movement contests, one per turn, until a terminal
+> condition is met:
+>
+> 1. **Contest each turn.** Both parties roll full Core Tests (DEC-006) on
+>    declared movement-relevant Skills (DEC-025/DEC-106; e.g., an
+>    athletics/evasion/pursuit-lineage Skill). Innate Movement Speed is NOT a
+>    roll engine: it caps change, it does not resolve contests (§3.2).
+> 2. **Band change from Quality.** The winner's Quality (DEC-031/DEC-107)
+>    moves the gap one band step per content boundary (band↔hex mapping per
+>    DEC-133.A R1/DEC-077.A). With the hex model (DEC-133), the winner closes
+>    (or opens) the gap by their Quality in hexes, capped by effective
+>    Movement Speed difference rules (below).
+> 3. **Movement Speed caps closing.** A pursuer may close at most their
+>    Effective Movement Speed in hexes per turn; a fleeer may open at most
+>    theirs. When both have equal effective MS, the contest's Quality is the
+>    only gap-changer; the Speed cap prevents runaway catches/escapes from
+>    raw statistics. (DEC-133(3); DEC-004.)
+> 4. **Terminal conditions (content per DEC-077.A):** (a) pursuer enters
+>    Engagement with the fleeer → Chase ends, melee exchange applies;
+>    (b) gap exceeds the pursuer's maximum closing range (content; e.g., the
+>    fleeer's cumulative Quality edge plus a content threshold) → fleeer
+>    escapes, Chase ends; (c) either party stops, is denied movement
+>    (DEC-122 stack), or a terrain/hazard boundary (content) ends the Chase.
+> 5. **Chase movement is the turn's movement.** Both parties' hexes moved
+>    during the Chase consume their Movement Distance for the turn (DEC-095);
+>    no additional movement remains for that turn.
+> 6. **Consumption** of the contests themselves: Fork C (§4.1).
+> 7. **Overtaking treatment:** if the pursuer's contest result would carry them
+>    INTO the fleeer's Engagement band, the Chase resolves into melee per
+>    rules as normal (Entry into Engagement is permitted, §6 Z1); the pursuer
+>    has won condition (a).
+
+Rationale: every roll is a full Core Test (Invariants 6/18; no no-roll engine);
+Speed remains mechanically meaningful as the cap, not the resolver; one
+substantive exchange per turn retained (DEC-095); relation from Quality to
+geography is explicit and content-mapped. [EC: designer rulings + mechanical
+facts cited; recommendation — this shape]
+
+### (b) Alternative framings
+
+- **Option K2 — Extended Test chase (DEC-067/068 machinery):** the Chase is one
+  Extended Test (target set by GM per DEC-070), each participant rolling
+  cumulative progress. Preserves Core Test economics, adds completion-target
+  abstraction; loses per-turn band interplay. Register support: DEC-067/068 are
+  non-canonical Extended Test proposals; the S-1/Extended relationship in the
+  locked frame is the S-1-adjacent primitive. Presented as a legitimate second
+  shape; choosing between K1 and K2 needs Tiwa (Q6). [EC: designer ruling —
+  DEC-013 vs Extended primitives advisory; recommendation]
+- **Option K3 — single decisive contest:** one S-1 roll decides catch/escape,
+  Quality sets the band delta. Cheapest; no pursuit texture; recommended only
+  for expedition-scale (non-tactical) play where per-turn chases are rare.
+  [EC: recommendation]
+- **Option K4 — Speed-vs-Speed deterministic (EXCLUDED):** comparing Movement
+  Speed values with no roll is architecturally forbidden: no Core Test →
+  no Cost/Overflow/XP/Double/Recovery material (Invariant 6/18; DEC-006;
+  proposals-§1 identity). Deterministic comparison may only cap the rolling
+  result (rule 3), never replace it. [EC: mechanical fact (Invariant 6/18),
+  recommendation (the exclusion inference)]
+
+### (c) Evidence classes & open questions
+
+- No empirical chase data (mirror-match playtest had no chase scenario;
+  replication F-05: the 45.30% Repeat rate finding warrants a follow-up before
+  chase pacing is tuned — [EC: empirical finding]).
+- Open: K1 vs K2 shape (Q6); terminal-condition thresholds (content);

+  one substantive action per turn, DEC-095; attack = the exchange, not the

+## 8. M4 — Generic movement contests (universal primitive)

+> **Generic movement contest.** Any movement-conflict situation not covered by
+> a named mechanic (Disengage §5, ZoC §6, Chase §7, Forced Movement §9,
+> Pin/Hold §10, Seize/Deny §11) — e.g., shoving past a blocker in a corridor,
+> muscling through a press, resisting a current, holding a doorway — resolves
+> as a single S-1 opposed contest (DEC-013) on each participant's declared
+> movement-relevant Skill (DEC-025 declared intent; DEC-106 GM accepts
+> applicable Skills; creatures use their content-defined Skill choices).

+> - **Win/Loss:** per the S-1 outcome matrix (DEC-013.4/13.5; ties → repeat).
+> - **Payload:** if a named mechanic covers the situation, that mechanic's
+>   payload applies. If none does, the winner achieves their declared positional
+>   intent (DEC-025) to the extent the loser's position allows, at the GM's
+>   adjudication; numerical magnitude (if any) is content (DEC-077.A) or the

+## 9. M5 — Forced Movement magnitude
+
+### (a) Candidate rules text (Option F1 — Tier-scaled hexes)
+
+> **Forced Movement (Position-tier Effect, DEC-023.A).** Upon winning a contest
+> and selecting this Effect, the victor displaces the target in a declared
+> direction (DEC-025):
+>
+> - **Magnitude:** the target moves **Y hexes**, where **Y = the Effect's
+>   Tier** = the causing Skill's Skill-Tier (DEC-107), in the declared
+>   direction. Band reading: content-mapped per DEC-133.A R1 (e.g., Y hexes =
+>   1 band, or 1 band per Y, at content's option).
+> - **Path legality:** the displacement must not pass through occupied hexes or
+>   prohibited boundaries (terrain/hazard per content, DEC-077.A). Displacement
+>   stops at the first obstruction; the target is not impaled or chain-shoved
+>   by default (chain reactions = content, Q12).
+> - **Mitigation:** the target may attempt Active Defense per the standard
+>   defense machinery (DEC-050/097/103 shape): a successful AD shreds initial
+>   magnitude and reduces the remainder by the AD Margin (DEC-103 step-1/step-2
+>   pattern); displacement = `max(0, Y − AD_shred − AD_Margin)` hexes. A failed
+>   AD provides no mitigation (DEC-097). This keeps the magnitude reading
+>   record-native and defense-interactive without touching the Wound channel
+>   (HP never changes from displacement itself; Impact/knock damage is a
+>   separate Effect selection per DEC-024).
+> - **Record form:** consistent with DEC-115/117, the outcome may be recorded
+>   as `Tier-Y Forced Movement, Magnitude −Y` for bookkeeping; the spatial
+>   payload is hexes moved, not a penalty to any attribute. (The Z = −Y
+>   convention names magnitude; displacement is the spatial payload — the
+>   DEC-115 form is reused as a recording convention, see open Q11.)
+> - **Denied targets:** a target whose Effective MS is 0 (DEC-122 stack:
+>   Restrained/Grappled/Stunned/Incapacitated) has no movement of their own,
+>   but is still a physical body: displacement applies unless a specific
+>   Condition rule forbids it (content question, Q12). Grappled-pair
+>   displacement is a separate open interaction (Q12; DEC-131 covers
+>   move-away, not third-party displacement).
+
+Rationale: magnitude from the already-ruled record Tier (DEC-107/115) gives
+predictable scaling with zero new economy; AD mitigation reuses the ruled
+defense channel; no Quality-as-magnitude (DEC-107 preserved); no Invariant-6/
+17 surface. [EC: designer rulings; recommendation — F1]

+>   each time).
+> - **Deny:** the victor declares the same area, but the *payload is a
+>   prohibition*: the target may not enter/pass through while the claim

# Candidate Implementations — Seven Consuming Mechanics (DEC-133.A R3)

**Status:** Non-canonical advisory. Candidate rules text for the seven consuming
mechanics left open by **DEC-133.A R3**. Drafted for the multi-LLM GDD pipeline;
no DEC is inferred or resolved hereby; nothing here is promoted, demoted, or
superseded.

> You are producing non-canonical advisory material only. Per this project's `governance/status-model.md` and the LLM Governance Rules, your output goes into `investigations/` or `proposals/`, is never Canonical, and must not silently resolve an open designer fork. Cite existing DEC IDs from `decision-register.md` where relevant. State your evidence class (mechanical fact / empirical finding / designer ruling / recommendation) for each claim.

---

## 1. Spec card (self-declared for this draft)

**Purpose.** Provide candidate implementations for the seven mechanics named as
open in **DEC-133.A R3**: Disengage, Zone of Control, Chase, generic movement
contests, Forced Movement magnitude, Pin/Hold Position resolution, Seize/Deny
Ground resolution. Each candidate must: (a) be expressible as rules text,
(b) carry an evidence class per claim, (c) present open designer forks rather
than silently collapsing them.

**Status.** Proposal paper (advisory). Not a locked rule. `proposals/` placement
per README directory map; no promotion step has been run. The 8-step Promotion

## 2. Constraint analysis (what any candidate must survive)

### 2.1 Invariant 6 — Cost equals the natural roll

Any movement mechanic that resolves through the S-1 opposed contest (DEC-013)
inherits Core Test costs automatically: each participant rolls a full Core Test
on the appropriate Skill; the natural roll is the cost from their pool
(PE/MP-style), not a flat or extra-movement surcharge. [EC: mechanical fact — Canonical §16 Invariant 6 + DEC-006/013]

A candidate that charges *movement* ("leaving Engagement costs 2 extra hexes
of Movement Distance") charges a cost *in position units*, not in the natural
roll. That is not itself an Invariant-6 violation — Invariant 6 governs the
Core Test transaction's cost channel — but it creates a *second cost channel*
in the same operation, which is exactly the kind of accumulation the R2
consumption fork has to rule on (see §4.1). [EC: recommendation]

### 2.2 Invariant 17 — no competing primary resource or progression economy

Nothing in any candidate below creates a stored pool, a per-scene counter, a
bankable token, or a second XP/progression channel. The only consumable in any
candidate is (a) the natural-roll cost of each Core Test, and (b) a candidate-
specific question of whether the *per-turn movement budget* is consumed by a
failed contest (DEC-133.A R2 — presently open, see §4.1). The per-turn movement
budget is ephemeral (expires at turn end), so consuming it does not create a
stored economy; it only sharpens the turn's opportunity cost. [EC: mechanical fact (Core Test cost channel); recommendation (ephemerality reading)]

### 2.3 DEC-024 / DEC-030 — one Effect per win, no graded effects

The Position-tier Effects (DEC-023.A) are selectable one per winning contest
(DEC-024). "Push 3 hexes AND knock prone" is therefore NOT available from one
win unless the cash-out structure (DEC-026 second-effect mechanic) is engaged.
Candidates below treat Forced Movement, Knock Prone, Seize/Deny Ground, and
Pin/Hold Position as mutually exclusive single selections per win. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-024/026]

None of the proposed Position Effects below has graded outcomes (DEC-030):
the win either produces the declared positional change or it does not; magnitude
is fixed by the mechanic, not bid by Quality. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-030]

### 2.4 DEC-123 — "never total" discipline

Movement-denial Conditions (Restrained/Grappled/Stunned/Incapacitated via
DEC-122/124/125/126) zero the *movement attribute*, but action declaration is
never made impossible (DEC-123). Positional mechanics must therefore never say
"you may not attempt X this turn" purely as an effect; they must say "your
Effective Movement Speed is 0 (or −Y)" or "attempting X is a contested roll you
must win." The candidates below respect this: Disengage/ZoC denial is expressed
as *contested-blocking*, never as a veto of the movement declaration itself.
[EC: designer ruling — DEC-123]

### 2.5 DEC-082.A R2 caution — "complete answer" territory

The movement-denial × Movement Speed question was ruled complete in
DEC-082.A R2 (via DEC-122/123/126/131). A new mechanic must NOT re-open the
"how much movement do denial Conditions allow" question; it must reuse the
existing record stack. This is the decisive constraint on Pin/Hold (see §9).
[EC: designer ruling — DEC-082.A R2]

## 3. Shared design substrate (used by all seven candidates)

### 3.1 Geometry: bands + hexes (DEC-133 Hybrid)

Movement is measured in hexes per turn: **Movement Distance per turn =
Effective Movement Speed**, with **1 MS = 1 hex per turn** (DEC-133(3)). The
band model (Engagement / Short / Long, etc.) remains available with band↔hex
boundaries as content-authoring (DEC-133.A R1, DEC-077.A). All positional
payload below is stated in hexes with a parenthetical band reading; exact band
names and their hex widths are content. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-133/133.A R1]

### 3.2 Every movement roll is a full Core Test

There is no "movement engine" separate from the common resolution engine
(Core Test Transaction, DEC-006; Invariant 18). In particular, a hypothetical
"Speed-vs-Speed with no roll" chase resolution is excluded by the identity
requirement of §1 of the proposals document ("every meaningful attempt uses the
common resolution engine") — it would produce no Cost, no Overflow, no XP, no
Double material, starving the progression economy (Invariant 17-adjacent harm;
error channel full of rolls with no natural-roll cost would be non-canonical).
[EC: mechanical fact (Core Test identity; Invariant 6/18); recommendation (exclusion reads directly from those)] The candidate Chase text below is therefore contest-shaped only.

### 3.3 Movement is free and bundled

Normal movement per turn is free (bundled, DEC-095) and does not consume an
action. One substantive action per turn = one S-1 exchange (DEC-095). Moving
DURING an exchange is movement; movement is not itself an action. All seven
mechanics below are compatible with "movement happens, then the turn's
substantive action (if any) resolves" — no mechanic below claims a second
action. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-095]

### 3.4 Effect selection machinery (DEC-107)

Winner of a contest selects ONE Effect their Skill and Skill-Tier permit.
Effect Tier = causing Skill's Skill-Tier. Quality (Margin/Blackjack/Hybrid,
DEC-031) is the tie-break and the success precondition (Quality ≥ 1), NOT a
magnitude dial. Position-tier Effects (DEC-023.A) are selectable when the
winning Skill's Tier qualifies for Position-tier (per DEC-023.A's tier
unlock: "gated tiers unlock as dependencies lock" — movement model now locked;
whether an additional Skill-Tier gate applies is an open fork, see §12 Q2).
[EC: designer ruling — DEC-107/023.A/031/133.A]
