## 4. Shared open forks (must NOT be resolved by this draft)

### 4.1 Fork C — contested-movement consumption (DEC-133.A R2)

When a movement contest is lost (or attempted), what does it consume?

- **Option 1 — nothing beyond the contest's own Core Test cost.** The mover
  still completes their declared movement on a win; on a loss, movement is
  simply denied/blocked per the mechanic, and the mover keeps their (now
  unusable-for-that-path) budget for other hexes.
- **Option 2 — the mover's remaining movement budget is spent on the attempt.**
  Declaring a contested move commits the movement; failure consumes the
  declared hexes' cost from the mover's turn budget (they stop short).
- **Option 3 — both parties' movement budgets are spent** (the defender also
  "used" their position/hexes to contest).
- **Option 4 — Quality-based consumption:** the loser's Quality is read as
  hexes of lost position (this makes Quality a magnitude dial — tension with
  DEC-107 focus; see §10 M5-alt-B for the same tension in forced movement).

Evidence: each option satisfies Invariant 6 (cost channel untouched) and
Invariant 17 (budget is ephemeral per turn, never stored). Options 2–4 change
tactical texture (fleeing becomes committing-channel risk); Option 1 makes
contesting cheap. No empirical playtest data distinguishes these yet — the
mirror-match playtest had no positional asymmetry and produced no movement-band
evidence at all. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-133.A R2 names the fork open; empirical finding — no relevant playtest data; recommendation — a purpose-built chase/disengage scenario is required before choosing]

### 4.2 Fork G — generic movement contest: what skill, what payload

Any contested movement should resolve S-1 on an appropriate Skill (DEC-013 +
multiple-applicable-skills / GM fiat per DEC-106). Whether the payload of a
generic contest win is (a) positional (hexes per the specific mechanic), or
(b) only pass/fail with the *specific* mechanic providing magnitude, is a
content fork (§8). [EC: designer ruling — DEC-013/106; recommendation — payload belongs to named mechanics, generic contest is the universal primitive]

### 4.3 Fork T — does an additional Skill-Tier gate apply to Position-tier Effects?

DEC-023.A's tier-unlock rule ("gated tiers unlock as dependencies lock") plus
the now-locked movement model suggests Position-tier selections are unlocked.
An alternative reading applies an extra Skill-Tier requirement (e.g., Tier ≥ 2
for positional payloads, mirroring DEC-041's gate for Location Index effects).
Not resolved here. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-023.A/DEC-041; recommendation — flagged for Tiwa, Q2 in §12]

## 5. M1 — Disengage

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option A — contested departure, default permissive)

> **Disengage.** Leaving an opponent's Engagement band during your movement is
> normally permitted (normal movement, DEC-095). If you declare movement that
> will take you out of an opponent's Engagement band, that opponent may contest
> the departure as a movement-trigger reaction (**if and only if** they hold an
> authored Tag in the `reaction:` movement-trigger category — DEC-132/132.A
> R1/132.B R3; content-authoring per DEC-077.A). The contest is a full S-1
> opposed contest (DEC-013): mover rolls their declared disengage Skill
> (e.g., an agility/evasion-lineage Skill per DEC-025 declared intent), defender
> rolls their declared reactive Skill.
>
> - **Mover wins:** departure succeeds; the mover completes the declared
>   movement (consumption per Fork C, §4.1).
> - **Defender wins:** the mover's movement for this turn ends at the boundary
>   of the Engagement band they attempted to leave; they may still perform
>   non-movement actions (DEC-095), may attempt a new disengage (another S-1,
>   another Core Test cost), or may abandon movement entirely. Movement is
>   denied by position, never by action-veto (DEC-123).
> - **No Tag, no reaction:** no contest; the departure is free normal movement
>   unless movement is otherwise denied (Grappled → DEC-124/131 break-hold
>   contest is required; Restrained/zeroed MS → normal movement is already 0).

Rationale trace: reaction-scoped (Tag-gated) so the framework adds no universal
"opportunity attack"; mover-equivocation of the outcome (positional denial, not
action denial) obeys DEC-123; one full S-1 contest per attempt (DEC-006/013);
consumption left open (Fork C). [EC: designer rulings above; recommendation — this shape] 

### (b) Alternative framings (not collapsed)

- **Option B — free leave + opponent option only (no contest on leave):**
  leaving Engagement is always free movement; the only cost the opponent can
  impose is a *separate* declared action (e.g., a Strike via their own
  substantive action), not a reaction. Simpler, but makes disengage trivially
  safe against melee — likely too weak a denial for ranged/pursuit play.
  [EC: recommendation]
- **Option C — movement-extra-cost model:** leaving Engagement costs +Y hexes
  of Movement Distance. Risk: this amends DEC-133(3)'s flat "1 MS = 1 hex"
  conversion per-hex — a per-path surcharge is a new movement arithmetic that
  DEC-133.family did not settle and that drifts toward a movement-point
  economy (Invariant 17 watch). Presented because "attack of opportunity →
  extra movement cost" is a genre-common pattern; not recommended as a clean
  fit for the locked movement frame. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-133(3) is flat 1:1; recommendation — flag; Invariant 17 caution]
- **Option D — auto-fail stance:** a defender *always* contests a disengage
  (no Tag needed). This converts disengage into a universal S-1 roll every
  time — heavier rolling; contradicts the reaction framework's tag-gated
  design intent (DEC-132(4): trigger menus are content, not framework-wide).
  [EC: designer ruling — DEC-132(4); recommendation]

### (c) Evidence classes & open questions

- Mechanical facts: Core Test identity (DEC-006/013); one substantive action
  (DEC-095); movement free/bundled; Grappled break-hold required (DEC-124/131).
- Designer rulings relied on: DEC-132 reaction shape, DEC-123, DEC-133.A R2 fork.
- No empirical evidence: mirror-match playtest had no disengage scenario.
- Open: (1) Fork C consumption; (2) Tag-authoring burden — should the movement-
  trigger category exist by default in the `reaction:` namespace for all
  combat-capable NPCs, or only where authored? [recommendation: per DEC-132(4)
  the namespace exists, tags are content; Q3 in §12]

## 6. M2 — Zone of Control (ZoC)

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option Z1 — permissive default + gated pass-through denial)

> **Zone of Control.** A combatant's ZoC is the hexes of their Engagement band
> (DEC-133 band model; band↔hex content per DEC-133.A R1).
>
> - **Entering** another combatant's Engagement band is always permitted (normal
>   movement) — no permission roll, no reaction by default.
> - **Passing through** an occupied Engagement band (entering and leaving it in
>   the same movement, with the intent to not stop inside it) may be contested
>   by the occupying combatant **if and only if** they hold an authored
>   movement-trigger Tag (same reaction machinery as Disengage, §5). On the
>   occupier's win, the mover's movement ends at the near boundary of the
>   contested band (positional denial, DEC-123-compliant) and the consumption
>   fork (§4.1) applies; on the mover's win, passage succeeds.
> - **No framework-level "no entry/no passage" law is created here.** Band
>   denial is either (i) tag-gated reaction machinery (above) or (ii) the
>   positional ownership effects of Seize/Deny Ground (§11). ZoC does not grant
>   free strikes: inflicting harm is a separate Effect selection (DEC-024) or a
>   declared action, never an automatic property of movement denial.
> - **Movement within** another combatant's Engagement band (e.g., circling to
>   flank) is a generic movement contest only when contested fiction demands it
>   (§8); otherwise it is normal movement.

Rationale: this is the minimal ZoC consistent with the locked frame — the
framework defines the *band* as the zone, and denies *passage* only through the
reaction machinery that the register already provides for movement triggers.
It avoids both (i) automatic free attacks (DEC-024/DEC-101 counter-Effect
prohibition) and (ii) a framework-level no-passage law that DEC-030/DEC-123 do
not license. [EC: designer rulings — DEC-024/101/123/132; recommendation]

### (b) Alternative framings

- **Option Z2 — restrictive default (genre-standard):** passing through an
  occupied Engagement band is *prohibited by default*; only a successful S-1
  contest (mover) allows passage. This is the D&D-style ZoC. It creates a
  universal denial law at the framework level — a heavier footprint than the
  register's tag-gated reaction design and gives every defender a free
  contest-denial without a Tag. Whether the designer wants this "sticky
  engagement" texture is exactly the open fork (Q4). [EC: recommendation]
- **Option Z3 — no framework ZoC at all:** ZoC = purely descriptive band
  geometry; all denial is content-authored (terrain, specific creature rules,
  Seize/Deny Ground Effects). Zero framework footprint; likely too weak for
  melee-front protection in a tactical game (no empirical data either way).
  [EC: recommendation; empirical finding — no playtest coverage of ZoC]
- **Option Z4 — ZoC as movement-suppression aura:** entities inside your
  Engagement band have their Effective Movement Speed reduced (−1 hex) while
  inside. This is a +Y overlay on Z = −Y machinery (DEC-115/138) — seductive,
  but it converts a *positional* rule into a *condition-like penalty* outside
  the Condition record system (DEC-079 alpha vocabulary), which the movement-
  denial closure (DEC-082.A R2) warns against. Presented, not recommended.
  [EC: designer ruling — DEC-082.A R2, DEC-138; recommendation]

### (c) Evidence classes & open questions

- Mechanical facts: band model from DEC-133(2); reaction machinery DEC-132.
- No empirical data (mirror-match playtest had no ZoC/pass-through scenario —
  [EC: empirical finding]).
- Open: permissive vs restrictive posture (Q4); whether entry-into-Engagement
  should also be tag-gated (recommendation: no — entry is the defender-friendly
  act; denial targets exit/passage); interplay with Seize/Deny Ground (§11).

## 7. M3 — Chase

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option K1 — sequential S-1 movement contests, band-driven)

> **Chase.** When one party (the FLEEER) moves with the declared intent to
> break off and the other (the PURSUER) declares pursuit as that turn's
> substantive action (DEC-095 — one S-1 exchange per turn), resolve a Chase as
> a sequence of S-1 opposed movement contests, one per turn, until a terminal
> condition is met:
>
> 1. **Contest each turn.** Both parties roll full Core Tests (DEC-006) on
>    declared movement-relevant Skills (DEC-025/DEC-106; e.g., an
>    athletics/evasion/pursuit-lineage Skill). Innate Movement Speed is NOT a
>    roll engine: it caps change, it does not resolve contests (§3.2).
> 2. **Band change from Quality.** The winner's Quality (DEC-031/DEC-107)
>    moves the gap one band step per content boundary (band↔hex mapping per
>    DEC-133.A R1/DEC-077.A). With the hex model (DEC-133), the winner closes
>    (or opens) the gap by their Quality in hexes, capped by effective
>    Movement Speed difference rules (below).
> 3. **Movement Speed caps closing.** A pursuer may close at most their
>    Effective Movement Speed in hexes per turn; a fleeer may open at most
>    theirs. When both have equal effective MS, the contest's Quality is the
>    only gap-changer; the Speed cap prevents runaway catches/escapes from
>    raw statistics. (DEC-133(3); DEC-004.)
> 4. **Terminal conditions (content per DEC-077.A):** (a) pursuer enters
>    Engagement with the fleeer → Chase ends, melee exchange applies;
>    (b) gap exceeds the pursuer's maximum closing range (content; e.g., the
>    fleeer's cumulative Quality edge plus a content threshold) → fleeer
>    escapes, Chase ends; (c) either party stops, is denied movement
>    (DEC-122 stack), or a terrain/hazard boundary (content) ends the Chase.
> 5. **Chase movement is the turn's movement.** Both parties' hexes moved
>    during the Chase consume their Movement Distance for the turn (DEC-095);
>    no additional movement remains for that turn.
> 6. **Consumption** of the contests themselves: Fork C (§4.1).
> 7. **Overtaking treatment:** if the pursuer's contest result would carry them
>    INTO the fleeer's Engagement band, the Chase resolves into melee per
>    rules as normal (Entry into Engagement is permitted, §6 Z1); the pursuer
>    has won condition (a).

Rationale: every roll is a full Core Test (Invariants 6/18; no no-roll engine);
Speed remains mechanically meaningful as the cap, not the resolver; one
substantive exchange per turn retained (DEC-095); relation from Quality to
geography is explicit and content-mapped. [EC: designer rulings + mechanical
facts cited; recommendation — this shape]

### (b) Alternative framings

- **Option K2 — Extended Test chase (DEC-067/068 machinery):** the Chase is one
  Extended Test (target set by GM per DEC-070), each participant rolling
  cumulative progress. Preserves Core Test economics, adds completion-target
  abstraction; loses per-turn band interplay. Register support: DEC-067/068 are
  non-canonical Extended Test proposals; the S-1/Extended relationship in the
  locked frame is the S-1-adjacent primitive. Presented as a legitimate second
  shape; choosing between K1 and K2 needs Tiwa (Q6). [EC: designer ruling —
  DEC-013 vs Extended primitives advisory; recommendation]
- **Option K3 — single decisive contest:** one S-1 roll decides catch/escape,
  Quality sets the band delta. Cheapest; no pursuit texture; recommended only
  for expedition-scale (non-tactical) play where per-turn chases are rare.
  [EC: recommendation]
- **Option K4 — Speed-vs-Speed deterministic (EXCLUDED):** comparing Movement
  Speed values with no roll is architecturally forbidden: no Core Test →
  no Cost/Overflow/XP/Double/Recovery material (Invariant 6/18; DEC-006;
  proposals-§1 identity). Deterministic comparison may only cap the rolling
  result (rule 3), never replace it. [EC: mechanical fact (Invariant 6/18),
  recommendation (the exclusion inference)]

### (c) Evidence classes & open questions

- No empirical chase data (mirror-match playtest had no chase scenario;
  replication F-05: the 45.30% Repeat rate finding warrants a follow-up before
  chase pacing is tuned — [EC: empirical finding]).
- Open: K1 vs K2 shape (Q6); terminal-condition thresholds (content);
  whether pursuer/ fleeer may also attack while chasing (recommendation: No —
  one substantive action per turn, DEC-095; attack = the exchange, not the
  chase-contest; the chase itself is the exchange).

## 8. M4 — Generic movement contests (universal primitive)

### (a) Candidate rules text

> **Generic movement contest.** Any movement-conflict situation not covered by
> a named mechanic (Disengage §5, ZoC §6, Chase §7, Forced Movement §10,
> Pin/Hold §9, Seize/Deny §11) — e.g., shoving past a blocker in a corridor,
> muscling through a press, resisting a current, holding a doorway — resolves
> as a single S-1 opposed contest (DEC-013) on each participant's declared
> movement-relevant Skill (DEC-025 declared intent; DEC-106 GM accepts
> applicable Skills; creatures use their content-defined Skill choices).
>
> - **Win/Loss:** per the S-1 outcome matrix (DEC-013.4/13.5; ties → repeat).
> - **Payload:** if a named mechanic covers the situation, that mechanic's
>   payload applies. If none does, the winner achieves their declared positional
>   intent (DEC-025) to the extent the loser's position allows, at the GM's
>   adjudication; numerical magnitude (if any) is content (DEC-077.A) or the
>   named-mechanic convention (Tier-scaled — see §10/§11).
> - **Consumption:** Fork C (§4.1).
> - **This is not a new system:** one full Core Test per participant, one
>   exchange, normal costs/XP/Doubles/Recovery (DEC-006/007/009/012).

Rationale: makes the "S-1 is the universal contested primitive" explicit for
movement without granting magnitude powers to the generic form (magnitude
belongs to named mechanics/or content — keeps DEC-030 discipline). [EC:
mechanical fact — DEC-013; designer rulings — DEC-025/106/077.A; recommendation]

### (b) Alternative framings

- **Option B — generic contest grants framework magnitude:** winner's Quality =
  hexes of position gained, universally. Risk: Quality-as-magnitude tension
  with DEC-107 (see §10 M5-alt-B) and unruled knock-on displacement. Not
  recommended; magnitude should stay with named mechanics (Q7). [EC:
  designer ruling — DEC-107; recommendation]
- **Option C — GM-fiat-only generic resolution (no roll template):** situations
  resolve by GM narrative + ad hoc rolls. Loses the uniform Core Test economics;
  rejected because the register's direction is universal S-1 primitives
  (DEC-013's role as "universal contested primitive"). [EC: recommendation]

### (c) Open questions

- Skill-selection edge: what counts as "movement-relevant" for non-physical
  characters (stealth-lineage evasion vs athletics-lineage dash) — content or a
  framework list? (Q8)
- Third-party adjudication (mutual failure / observer interference) is outside
  this draft's scope (register references S-8 patterns non-canonically — not
  relied on here).

## 9. M5 (as listed in DEC-133.A R3, "pin/hold position") — see §9.1 below: Pin/Hold Position

> NOTE: The register's seven-item list reads: Disengage, Zone of Control,
> Chase, generic movement contests, **Forced Movement magnitude**, **Pin/Hold
> Position resolution**, **Seize/Deny Ground resolution**. §9 is Pin/Hold;
> Forced Movement magnitude is §10; Seize/Deny is §11.

### 9.1 Pin/Hold Position — (a) Candidate rules text (Option P1 — route to existing Condition machinery)

> **Pin / Hold Position (Position-tier Effect, DEC-023.A).** Upon winning a
> contest and selecting this Effect (DEC-024/107), the victor imposes the
> existing **Restrained** Condition record on the target (DEC-079 alpha
> vocabulary; DEC-115/117 record form: `Tier-Y Restrained, Magnitude Z = −Y`,
> Location per the declared fiction / DEC-023.A(3) gating):
>
> - **Record:** `Tier-Y Restrained` where Y = the causing Skill's Skill-Tier

Rationale: maximum reuse of the ruled Condition stack (DEC-079/115/122/123/
124/125/126/131); honors DEC-082.A R2's "complete answer" closure by NOT
creating a parallel denial Condition; the record form is already the unified
pattern (DEC-115/117). [EC: designer rulings; recommendation — P1]

### (b) Alternative framings

- **Option P2 — new alpha Condition "Pinned/Held":** author a NEW Condition
  into the DEC-079 vocabulary (amendment process; alpha condition vocabulary

  status; DEC-082.A R2; recommendation — heavier, only if Tiwa wants distinct
  Pinned mechanics]

  purely as geometry ("target may not leave the band while the pinner
  maintains the hold") without a Restrained record. Deceptively simple; fails
  because "may not leave the band" is movement denial that the locked stack
  expresses via the record overlay (DEC-122) — inventing a geometry-only denial
  re-opens the closed movement-denial question. [EC: designer ruling —
  DEC-082.A R2/122; recommendation]

  with a dedicated record name routed through Condition-resolution. This is a
  labeling fork, not a mechanics fork; name choice is content (Q9).

### (c) Evidence classes & open questions

- Mechanical facts: Condition record machinery (DEC-115/117/122/131).
- No empirical evidence distinguishing P1–P4 (no hold/pin playtest).
- Open: (1) P1 vs P2 (new Condition amendment) — Q9; (2) does the pinner
  sacrifice their own movement while holding (recommendation: yes — holding
  engages the pinner's position; this is the natural reading of "Hold
  Position," but it should be stated explicitly if adopted) — Q10; (3) can
  allies carry/pull a Restrained target out of the pin (recommendation: yes,
  via the escape contest machinery, not free drag).

---

## 10. Forced Movement magnitude

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option F1 — Tier-scaled hexes)

> **Forced Movement (Position-tier Effect, DEC-023.A).** Upon winning a contest
> and selecting this Effect, the victor displaces the target in a declared
> direction (DEC-025):
>
> - **Magnitude:** the target moves **Y hexes**, where **Y = the Effect's
>   Tier** = the causing Skill's Skill-Tier (DEC-107), in the declared
>   direction. Band reading: content-mapped per DEC-133.A R1 (e.g., Y hexes =
>   1 band, or 1 band per Y, at content's option).
> - **Path legality:** the displacement must not pass through occupied hexes or
>   prohibited boundaries (terrain/hazard per content, DEC-077.A). Displacement
>   stops at the first obstruction; the target is not impaled or chain-shoved
>   by default (chain reactions = content, Q12).
> - **Mitigation:** the target may attempt Active Defense per the standard
>   defense machinery (DEC-050/097/103 shape): a successful AD shreds initial
>   magnitude and reduces the remainder by the AD Margin (DEC-103 step-1/step-2
>   pattern); displacement = `max(0, Y − AD_shred − AD_Margin)` hexes. A failed
>   AD provides no mitigation (DEC-097). This keeps the magnitude reading
>   record-native and defense-interactive without touching the Wound channel
>   (HP never changes from displacement itself; Impact/knock damage is a
>   separate Effect selection per DEC-024).
> - **Record form:** consistent with DEC-115/117, the outcome may be recorded
>   as `Tier-Y Forced Movement, Magnitude −Y` for bookkeeping; the spatial
>   payload is hexes moved, not a penalty to any attribute. (The Z = −Y
>   convention names magnitude; displacement is the spatial payload — the
>   DEC-115 form is reused as a recording convention, see open Q11.)
> - **Denied targets:** a target whose Effective MS is 0 (DEC-122 stack:
>   Restrained/Grappled/Stunned/Incapacitated) has no movement of their own,
>   but is still a physical body: displacement applies unless a specific
>   Condition rule forbids it (content question, Q12). Grappled-pair
>   displacement is a separate open interaction (Q12; DEC-131 covers
>   move-away, not third-party displacement).

Rationale: magnitude from the already-ruled record Tier (DEC-107/115) gives
predictable scaling with zero new economy; AD mitigation reuses the ruled
defense channel; no Quality-as-magnitude (DEC-107 preserved); no Invariant-6/
17 surface. [EC: designer rulings; recommendation — F1]

### (b) Alternative framings

- **Option F2 — Quality/Margin-scaled displacement:** target moves the
  winner's Quality in hexes (clamped by content). More dramatic swings; makes
  Quality a magnitude dial — direct tension with DEC-107 (Quality = tie-break

  chosen (Q11). [EC: designer ruling — DEC-107; recommendation — prefer F1]

  under DEC-077.A content-authoring if Tiwa wants per-skill tables. [EC:
  empirical finding — G1/G3 brief tables exist for penalties, not displacements;
  recommendation]
- **Option F4 — contest-delta (winner margin − loser margin) as hexes** (the
  DEC-103/104 wound-channel shape): consistent with Wound magnitude
  conventions; but again reads margins as magnitude — same DEC-107 tension as
  F2. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-103/104 (wound channel); recommendation]

### (c) Open questions

- Q11: F1 (Tier-scaled) vs F2/F4 (margin-scaled) — the magnitude source fork;
  and the "record form vs spatial payload" terminology question.
- Q12: obstruction/chain-shove defaults; displacement of DEC-122-zeroed and
  Grappled targets.
- Q13: does displacement provoke its own movement-trigger reactions (e.g., a
  third party reacting to the displaced entity entering their band) — recommend
  Yes via the same tag-gated machinery, consistent with §6.

---

## 11. Seize/Deny Ground resolution

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option S1 — position-ownership model)

> **Seize / Deny Ground (Position-tier Effect, DEC-023.A).** Upon winning a
> contest and selecting this Effect, the victor declares a ground claim:
>
> - **Seize:** the victor declares a band/hex area (hostile Occupancy declared
>   per DEC-025). The target is displaced out of that area by **Y hexes**
>   (same Tier-scaled magnitude as Forced Movement, §10 — one convention for
>   positional payloads), and the victor occupies it. The loser may not re-enter
>   or pass through the seized area without winning a new contest (an M4
>   generic movement contest, or the §6 ZoC machinery if a movement-trigger Tag
>   applies — both are S-1, repeated attempts allowed with natural-roll costs
>   each time).
> - **Deny:** the victor declares the same area, but the *payload is a
>   prohibition*: the target may not enter/pass through while the claim
>   stands; entering is contested (as above). Deny is Seize with the
>   displacement step omitted — one resolution, two declared intents.
> - **Binary outcomes only (DEC-030):** no graded claims; a single win either
>   establishes the claimed position or does not. Duration is open to content
>   (until contested, until the victor leaves, or a content-set term — Q14).

>   separate Effect selections (DEC-024); a win that Seizes has already spent
>   its Effect slot and does not also displace via Forced Movement rules.

convention (§10) for consistency; strictly binary (DEC-030); interacts cleanly

recommendation — S1]

  stops instant re-entry beyond a generic contest. [EC: recommendation]

  band-general form and Open/Close Lane (DEC-023.A's positional sibling) as
  the directional form, sharing §11's resolution. Recommended as a
  consolidation to propose to Tiwa (Q15) — not silently merged here.

  accumulate; explicitly NOT recommended — persistent position-tokens would
  drift into a stored economy (Invariant 17 watch) and violate the ephemerality
  principle of the movement frame. [EC: recommendation; Invariant 17 caution]

- Q14: claim duration (until re-contested vs content-set).

  themselves (also Position-tier alpha, also unruled — same candidate shape
  applies: directional band claim + re-entry contest).

  movement action (e.g., teleport/transport effects)? Recommend: content per

# Candidate Implementations — Seven Consuming Mechanics (DEC-133.A R3)

**Status:** Non-canonical advisory. Candidate rules text for the seven consuming
mechanics left open by **DEC-133.A R3**. Drafted for the multi-LLM GDD pipeline;
no DEC is inferred or resolved hereby; nothing here is promoted, demoted, or
superseded.

> You are producing non-canonical advisory material only. Per this project's `governance/status-model.md` and the LLM Governance Rules, your output goes into `investigations/` or `proposals/`, is never Canonical, and must not silently resolve an open designer fork. Cite existing DEC IDs from `decision-register.md` where relevant. State your evidence class (mechanical fact / empirical finding / designer ruling / recommendation) for each claim.

---

## 1. Spec card (self-declared for this draft)

**Purpose.** Provide candidate implementations for the seven mechanics named as
open in **DEC-133.A R3**: Disengage, Zone of Control, Chase, generic movement
contests, Forced Movement magnitude, Pin/Hold Position resolution, Seize/Deny
Ground resolution. Each candidate must: (a) be expressible as rules text,
(b) carry an evidence class per claim, (c) present open designer forks rather
than silently collapsing them.

**Status.** Proposal paper (advisory). Not a locked rule. `proposals/` placement
per README directory map; no promotion step has been run. The 8-step Promotion
Rule (REQ-021; `governance/status-model.md`) has NOT been applied to anything
here.

**Dependency chain (what this draft builds on).**

| Dependency | Status | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical Rules v1.3 §16 Core Architectural Invariants | Canonical/Locked | Constraint set, esp. Invariants 6, 17, 18 |
| DEC-004 (Movement Speed derived stat) | Canonical/Locked | Base constant for movement quantity |
| DEC-006 (9-step Core Test Transaction) | Canonical/Locked | Every movement roll is a full Core Test |
| DEC-013 (S-1 Opposed Contest primitive) | Canonical/Locked | Universal opposed resolution |
| DEC-023.A (Position-tier Effects alpha list) | Designer ruling (register) | Menu shell the R3 mechanics sit under |
| DEC-095 (movement free/bundled; one substantive action per turn) | Designer ruling (register) | Turn-economy frame |
| DEC-107 (Effect Tier = Skill-Tier; Quality = tie-break + success precondition) | Designer ruling (register) | Effect-selection machinery |
| DEC-122/124/125/126/131 (movement-denial machinery; Grappled break-hold; no move-away relocation) | Designer rulings (register) | Denial/confinement boundary cases |
| DEC-132/132.A/132.B (reactions; movement-trigger category, tag-gated) | Designer rulings (register) | Reaction machinery for Disengage/ZoC |
| DEC-133 (Movement Distance/turn = effective MS; 1 MS = 1 hex/turn; band model) | Designer ruling (register) | Movement quantity/geometry frame |
| DEC-133.A R1–R3 (band↔hex content-authoring; contested-movement consumption open; the seven mechanics open) | Designer ruling (register) | The direct mandate for this draft |
| DEC-115 (Z = −Y magnitude convention), DEC-138 (uniform −Y overlay) | Designer rulings (register) | Magnitude conventions |

Evidence class: the dependency table is a **mechanical fact** insofar as it
reports registry status; the status values themselves are **designer rulings**
recorded in the register `_consolidation/decision-register.md`.

**Locked invariants respected (constraint sheet).** Invariant 6 (Cost = natural
roll), Invariant 17 (no competing primary resource/progression economy),
Invariant 18 (no subsystem may replace the Core Test Transaction), DEC-024
(one Effect per win), DEC-030 (no graded outcomes; fail-and-fall-back only for
Tag/Location-gated Effects), DEC-095 (movement bundled; one substantive action),
DEC-123 ("never total" — no mechanic may make action declaration impossible),
DEC-115 Z = −Y, DEC-138 uniform overlay.

**Open questions (carried, not answered here).** See §4 (shared forks) and §12
(designer question list). Chief among them: contested-movement consumption
(DEC-133.A R2), ZoC posture (permissive vs restrictive), Forced Movement
magnitude source (Tier vs Margin vs content), Pin/Hold routing (existing
Condition vs new Condition), Chase resolution shape.

---

## 2. Constraint analysis (what any candidate must survive)

### 2.1 Invariant 6 — Cost equals the natural roll

Any movement mechanic that resolves through the S-1 opposed contest (DEC-013)
inherits Core Test costs automatically: each participant rolls a full Core Test
on the appropriate Skill; the natural roll is the cost from their pool
(PE/MP-style), not a flat or extra-movement surcharge. [EC: mechanical fact — Canonical §16 Invariant 6 + DEC-006/013]

A candidate that charges *movement* ("leaving Engagement costs 2 extra hexes
of Movement Distance") charges a cost *in position units*, not in the natural
roll. That is not itself an Invariant-6 violation — Invariant 6 governs the
Core Test transaction's cost channel — but it creates a *second cost channel*
in the same operation, which is exactly the kind of accumulation the R2
consumption fork has to rule on (see §4.1). [EC: recommendation]

### 2.2 Invariant 17 — no competing primary resource or progression economy

Nothing in any candidate below creates a stored pool, a per-scene counter, a
bankable token, or a second XP/progression channel. The only consumable in any
candidate is (a) the natural-roll cost of each Core Test, and (b) a candidate-
specific question of whether the *per-turn movement budget* is consumed by a
failed contest (DEC-133.A R2 — presently open, see §4.1). The per-turn movement
budget is ephemeral (expires at turn end), so consuming it does not create a
stored economy; it only sharpens the turn's opportunity cost. [EC: mechanical fact (Core Test cost channel); recommendation (ephemerality reading)]

### 2.3 DEC-024 / DEC-030 — one Effect per win, no graded effects

The Position-tier Effects (DEC-023.A) are selectable one per winning contest
(DEC-024). "Push 3 hexes AND knock prone" is therefore NOT available from one
win unless the cash-out structure (DEC-026 second-effect mechanic) is engaged.
Candidates below treat Forced Movement, Knock Prone, Seize/Deny Ground, and
Pin/Hold Position as mutually exclusive single selections per win. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-024/026]

None of the proposed Position Effects below has graded outcomes (DEC-030):
the win either produces the declared positional change or it does not; magnitude
is fixed by the mechanic, not bid by Quality. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-030]

### 2.4 DEC-123 — "never total" discipline

Movement-denial Conditions (Restrained/Grappled/Stunned/Incapacitated via
DEC-122/124/125/126) zero the *movement attribute*, but action declaration is
never made impossible (DEC-123). Positional mechanics must therefore never say
"you may not attempt X this turn" purely as an effect; they must say "your
Effective Movement Speed is 0 (or −Y)" or "attempting X is a contested roll you
must win." The candidates below respect this: Disengage/ZoC denial is expressed
as *contested-blocking*, never as a veto of the movement declaration itself.
[EC: designer ruling — DEC-123]

### 2.5 DEC-082.A R2 caution — "complete answer" territory

The movement-denial × Movement Speed question was ruled complete in
DEC-082.A R2 (via DEC-122/123/126/131). A new mechanic must NOT re-open the
"how much movement do denial Conditions allow" question; it must reuse the
existing record stack. This is the decisive constraint on Pin/Hold (see §9).
[EC: designer ruling — DEC-082.A R2]

---

## 3. Shared design substrate (used by all seven candidates)

### 3.1 Geometry: bands + hexes (DEC-133 Hybrid)

Movement is measured in hexes per turn: **Movement Distance per turn =
Effective Movement Speed**, with **1 MS = 1 hex per turn** (DEC-133(3)). The
band model (Engagement / Short / Long, etc.) remains available with band↔hex
boundaries as content-authoring (DEC-133.A R1, DEC-077.A). All positional
payload below is stated in hexes with a parenthetical band reading; exact band
names and their hex widths are content. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-133/133.A R1]

### 3.2 Every movement roll is a full Core Test

There is no "movement engine" separate from the common resolution engine
(Core Test Transaction, DEC-006; Invariant 18). In particular, a hypothetical
"Speed-vs-Speed with no roll" chase resolution is excluded by the identity
requirement of §1 of the proposals document ("every meaningful attempt uses the
common resolution engine") — it would produce no Cost, no Overflow, no XP, no
Double material, starving the progression economy (Invariant 17-adjacent harm;
error channel full of rolls with no natural-roll cost would be non-canonical).
[EC: mechanical fact (Core Test identity; Invariant 6/18); recommendation (exclusion reads directly from those)] The candidate Chase text below is therefore contest-shaped only.

### 3.3 Movement is free and bundled

Normal movement per turn is free (bundled, DEC-095) and does not consume an
action. One substantive action per turn = one S-1 exchange (DEC-095). Moving
DURING an exchange is movement; movement is not itself an action. All seven
mechanics below are compatible with "movement happens, then the turn's
substantive action (if any) resolves" — no mechanic below claims a second
action. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-095]

### 3.4 Effect selection machinery (DEC-107)

Winner of a contest selects ONE Effect their Skill and Skill-Tier permit.
Effect Tier = causing Skill's Skill-Tier. Quality (Margin/Blackjack/Hybrid,
DEC-031) is the tie-break and the success precondition (Quality ≥ 1), NOT a
magnitude dial. Position-tier Effects (DEC-023.A) are selectable when the
winning Skill's Tier qualifies for Position-tier (per DEC-023.A's tier
unlock: "gated tiers unlock as dependencies lock" — movement model now locked;
whether an additional Skill-Tier gate applies is an open fork, see §12 Q2).
[EC: designer ruling — DEC-107/023.A/031/133.A]

---

## 4. Shared open forks (must NOT be resolved by this draft)

## 2. Constraint analysis (what any candidate must survive)

### 2.1 Invariant 6 — Cost equals the natural roll

Any movement mechanic that resolves through the S-1 opposed contest (DEC-013)
inherits Core Test costs automatically: each participant rolls a full Core Test
on the appropriate Skill; the natural roll is the cost from their pool
(PE/MP-style), not a flat or extra-movement surcharge. [EC: mechanical fact — Canonical §16 Invariant 6 + DEC-006/013]

A candidate that charges *movement* ("leaving Engagement costs 2 extra hexes
of Movement Distance") charges a cost *in position units*, not in the natural
roll. That is not itself an Invariant-6 violation — Invariant 6 governs the
Core Test transaction's cost channel — but it creates a *second cost channel*
in the same operation, which is exactly the kind of accumulation the R2
consumption fork has to rule on (see §4.1). [EC: recommendation]

### 2.2 Invariant 17 — no competing primary resource or progression economy

Nothing in any candidate below creates a stored pool, a per-scene counter, a
bankable token, or a second XP/progression channel. The only consumable in any
candidate is (a) the natural-roll cost of each Core Test, and (b) a candidate-
specific question of whether the *per-turn movement budget* is consumed by a
failed contest (DEC-133.A R2 — presently open, see §4.1). The per-turn movement
budget is ephemeral (expires at turn end), so consuming it does not create a
stored economy; it only sharpens the turn's opportunity cost. [EC: mechanical fact (Core Test cost channel); recommendation (ephemerality reading)]

### 2.3 DEC-024 / DEC-030 — one Effect per win, no graded effects

The Position-tier Effects (DEC-023.A) are selectable one per winning contest
(DEC-024). "Push 3 hexes AND knock prone" is therefore NOT available from one
win unless the cash-out structure (DEC-026 second-effect mechanic) is engaged.
Candidates below treat Forced Movement, Knock Prone, Seize/Deny Ground, and
Pin/Hold Position as mutually exclusive single selections per win. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-024/026]

None of the proposed Position Effects below has graded outcomes (DEC-030):
the win either produces the declared positional change or it does not; magnitude
is fixed by the mechanic, not bid by Quality. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-030]

### 2.4 DEC-123 — "never total" discipline

Movement-denial Conditions (Restrained/Grappled/Stunned/Incapacitated via
DEC-122/124/125/126) zero the *movement attribute*, but action declaration is
never made impossible (DEC-123). Positional mechanics must therefore never say
"you may not attempt X this turn" purely as an effect; they must say "your
Effective Movement Speed is 0 (or −Y)" or "attempting X is a contested roll you
must win." The candidates below respect this: Disengage/ZoC denial is expressed
as *contested-blocking*, never as a veto of the movement declaration itself.
[EC: designer ruling — DEC-123]

### 2.5 DEC-082.A R2 caution — "complete answer" territory

The movement-denial × Movement Speed question was ruled complete in
DEC-082.A R2 (via DEC-122/123/126/131). A new mechanic must NOT re-open the
"how much movement do denial Conditions allow" question; it must reuse the
existing record stack. This is the decisive constraint on Pin/Hold (see §10).
[EC: designer ruling — DEC-082.A R2]

## 3. Shared design substrate (used by all seven candidates)

### 3.1 Geometry: bands + hexes (DEC-133 Hybrid)

Movement is measured in hexes per turn: **Movement Distance per turn =
Effective Movement Speed**, with **1 MS = 1 hex per turn** (DEC-133(3)). The
band model (Engagement / Short / Long, etc.) remains available with band↔hex
boundaries as content-authoring (DEC-133.A R1, DEC-077.A). All positional
payload below is stated in hexes with a parenthetical band reading; exact band
names and their hex widths are content. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-133/133.A R1]

### 3.2 Every movement roll is a full Core Test

There is no "movement engine" separate from the common resolution engine
(Core Test Transaction, DEC-006; Invariant 18). In particular, a hypothetical
"Speed-vs-Speed with no roll" chase resolution is excluded by the identity
requirement of §1 of the proposals document ("every meaningful attempt uses the
common resolution engine") — it would produce no Cost, no Overflow, no XP, no
Double material, starving the progression economy (Invariant 17-adjacent harm;
an error channel full of rolls with no natural-roll cost would be non-canonical).
[EC: mechanical fact (Core Test identity; Invariant 6/18); recommendation (exclusion reads directly from those)] The candidate Chase text below is therefore contest-shaped only.

### 3.3 Movement is free and bundled

Normal movement per turn is free (bundled, DEC-095) and does not consume an
action. One substantive action per turn = one S-1 exchange (DEC-095). Moving
DURING an exchange is movement; movement is not itself an action. All seven
mechanics below are compatible with "movement happens, then the turn's
substantive action (if any) resolves" — no mechanic below claims a second
action. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-095]

### 3.4 Effect selection machinery (DEC-107)

Winner of a contest selects ONE Effect their Skill and Skill-Tier permit.
Effect Tier = causing Skill's Skill-Tier. Quality (Margin/Blackjack/Hybrid,
DEC-031) is the tie-break and the success precondition (Quality ≥ 1), NOT a
magnitude dial. Position-tier Effects (DEC-023.A) are selectable when the
winning Skill's Tier qualifies for Position-tier (per DEC-023.A's tier
unlock: "gated tiers unlock as dependencies lock" — movement model now locked;
whether an additional Skill-Tier gate applies is an open fork, see §12 Q2).
[EC: designer ruling — DEC-107/023.A/031/133.A]

## 4. Shared open forks (must NOT be resolved by this draft)

### 4.1 Fork C — contested-movement consumption (DEC-133.A R2)

When a movement contest is lost (or attempted), what does it consume?

- **Option 1 — nothing beyond the contest's own Core Test cost.** The mover
  still completes their declared movement on a win; on a loss, movement is
  simply denied/blocked per the mechanic, and the mover keeps their (now
  unusable-for-that-path) budget for other hexes.
- **Option 2 — the mover's remaining movement budget is spent on the attempt.**
  Declaring a contested move commits the movement; failure consumes the
  declared hexes' cost from the mover's turn budget (they stop short).
- **Option 3 — both parties' movement budgets are spent** (the defender also
  "used" their position/hexes to contest).
- **Option 4 — Quality-based consumption:** the loser's Quality is read as
  hexes of lost position (this makes Quality a magnitude dial — tension with
  DEC-107 focus; see §9 M5-alt-B for the same tension in forced movement).

Evidence: each option satisfies Invariant 6 (cost channel untouched) and
Invariant 17 (budget is ephemeral per turn, never stored). Options 2–4 change
tactical texture (fleeing becomes committing-channel risk); Option 1 makes
contesting cheap. No empirical playtest data distinguishes these yet — the
mirror-match playtest had no positional asymmetry and produced no movement-band
evidence at all. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-133.A R2 names the fork open; empirical finding — no relevant playtest data; recommendation — a purpose-built chase/disengage scenario is required before choosing]

### 4.2 Fork G — generic movement contest: what skill, what payload

Any contested movement should resolve S-1 on an appropriate Skill (DEC-013 +
multiple-applicable-skills / GM fiat per DEC-106). Whether the payload of a
generic contest win is (a) positional (hexes per the specific mechanic), or
(b) only pass/fail with the *specific* mechanic providing magnitude, is a
content fork (§8). [EC: designer ruling — DEC-013/106; recommendation — payload belongs to named mechanics, generic contest is the universal primitive]

### 4.3 Fork T — does an additional Skill-Tier gate apply to Position-tier Effects?

DEC-023.A's tier-unlock rule ("gated tiers unlock as dependencies lock") plus
the now-locked movement model suggests Position-tier selections are unlocked.
An alternative reading applies an extra Skill-Tier requirement (e.g., Tier ≥ 2
for positional payloads, mirroring DEC-041's gate for Location Index effects).
Not resolved here. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-023.A/DEC-041; recommendation — flagged for Tiwa, Q2 in §12]

## 5. M1 — Disengage

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option A — contested departure, default permissive)

> **Disengage.** Leaving an opponent's Engagement band during your movement is
> normally permitted (normal movement, DEC-095). If you declare movement that
> will take you out of an opponent's Engagement band, that opponent may contest
> the departure as a movement-trigger reaction (**if and only if** they hold an
> authored Tag in the `reaction:` movement-trigger category — DEC-132/132.A
> R1/132.B R3; content-authoring per DEC-077.A). The contest is a full S-1
> opposed contest (DEC-013): mover rolls their declared disengage Skill
> (e.g., an agility/evasion-lineage Skill per DEC-025 declared intent), defender
> rolls their declared reactive Skill.
>
> - **Mover wins:** departure succeeds; the mover completes the declared
>   movement (consumption per Fork C, §4.1).
> - **Defender wins:** the mover's movement for this turn ends at the boundary
>   of the Engagement band they attempted to leave; they may still perform
>   non-movement actions (DEC-095), may attempt a new disengage (another S-1,
>   another Core Test cost), or may abandon movement entirely. Movement is
>   denied by position, never by action-veto (DEC-123).
> - **No Tag, no reaction:** no contest; the departure is free normal movement
>   unless movement is otherwise denied (Grappled → DEC-124/131 break-hold
>   contest is required; Restrained/zeroed MS → normal movement is already 0).

Rationale trace: reaction-scoped (Tag-gated) so the framework adds no universal
"opportunity attack"; mover-equivocation of the outcome (positional denial, not
action denial) obeys DEC-123; one full S-1 contest per attempt (DEC-006/013);
consumption left open (Fork C). [EC: designer rulings above; recommendation — this shape] 

### (b) Alternative framings (not collapsed)

- **Option B — free leave + opponent option only (no contest on leave):**
  leaving Engagement is always free movement; the only cost the opponent can
  impose is a *separate* declared action (e.g., a Strike via their own
  substantive action), not a reaction. Simpler, but makes disengage trivially
  safe against melee — likely too weak a denial for ranged/pursuit play.
  [EC: recommendation]
- **Option C — movement-extra-cost model:** leaving Engagement costs +Y hexes
  of Movement Distance. Risk: this amends DEC-133(3)'s flat "1 MS = 1 hex"
  conversion per-hex — a per-path surcharge is a new movement arithmetic that
  DEC-133.family did not settle and that drifts toward a movement-point
  economy (Invariant 17 watch). Presented because "attack of opportunity →
  extra movement cost" is a genre-common pattern; not recommended as a clean
  fit for the locked movement frame. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-133(3) is flat 1:1; recommendation — flag; Invariant 17 caution]
- **Option D — auto-fail stance:** a defender *always* contests a disengage
  (no Tag needed). This converts disengage into a universal S-1 roll every
  time — heavier rolling; contradicts the reaction framework's tag-gated
  design intent (DEC-132(4): trigger menus are content, not framework-wide).
  [EC: designer ruling — DEC-132(4); recommendation]

### (c) Evidence classes & open questions

- Mechanical facts: Core Test identity (DEC-006/013); one substantive action
  (DEC-095); movement free/bundled; Grappled break-hold required (DEC-124/131).
- Designer rulings relied on: DEC-132 reaction shape, DEC-123, DEC-133.A R2 fork.
- No empirical evidence: mirror-match playtest had no disengage scenario.
- Open: (1) Fork C consumption; (2) Tag-authoring burden — should the movement-
  trigger category exist by default in the `reaction:` namespace for all

## 6. M2 — Zone of Control (ZoC)

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option Z1 — permissive default + gated pass-through denial)

> **Zone of Control.** A combatant's ZoC is the hexes of their Engagement band
> (DEC-133 band model; band↔hex content per DEC-133.A R1).
>
> - **Entering** another combatant's Engagement band is always permitted (normal
>   movement) — no permission roll, no reaction by default.
> - **Passing through** an occupied Engagement band (entering and leaving it in
>   the same movement, with the intent to not stop inside it) may be contested
>   by the occupying combatant **if and only if** they hold an authored
>   movement-trigger Tag (same reaction machinery as Disengage, §5). On the
>   occupier's win, the mover's movement ends at the near boundary of the
>   contested band (positional denial, DEC-123-compliant) and the consumption
>   fork (§4.1) applies; on the mover's win, passage succeeds.
> - **No framework-level "no entry/no passage" law is created here.** Band
>   denial is either (i) tag-gated reaction machinery (above) or (ii) the
>   positional ownership effects of Seize/Deny Ground (§11). ZoC does not grant
>   free strikes: inflicting harm is a separate Effect selection (DEC-024) or a
>   declared action, never an automatic property of movement denial.
> - **Movement within** another combatant's Engagement band (e.g., circling to
>   flank) is a generic movement contest only when contested fiction demands it
>   (§8); otherwise it is normal movement.

Rationale: this is the minimal ZoC consistent with the locked frame — the
framework defines the *band* as the zone, and denies *passage* only through the
reaction machinery that the register already provides for movement triggers.
It avoids both (i) automatic free attacks (DEC-024/DEC-101 counter-Effect
prohibition) and (ii) a framework-level no-passage law that DEC-030/DEC-123 do
not license. [EC: designer rulings — DEC-024/101/123/132; recommendation]

### (b) Alternative framings

- **Option Z2 — restrictive default (genre-standard):** passing through an
  occupied Engagement band is *prohibited by default*; only a successful S-1
  contest (mover) allows passage. This is the D&D-style ZoC. It creates a
  universal denial law at the framework level — a heavier footprint than the
  register's tag-gated reaction design and gives every defender a free
  contest-denial without a Tag. Whether the designer wants this "sticky
  engagement" texture is exactly the open fork (Q4). [EC: recommendation]
- **Option Z3 — no framework ZoC at all:** ZoC = purely descriptive band
  geometry; all denial is content-authored (terrain, specific creature rules,
  Seize/Deny Ground Effects). Zero framework footprint; likely too weak for
  melee-front protection in a tactical game (no empirical data either way).
  [EC: recommendation; empirical finding — no playtest coverage of ZoC]
- **Option Z4 — ZoC as movement-suppression aura:** entities inside your
  Engagement band have their Effective Movement Speed reduced (−1 hex) while
  inside. This is a +Y overlay on Z = −Y machinery (DEC-115/138) — seductive,
  but it converts a *positional* rule into a *condition-like penalty* outside
  the Condition record system (DEC-079 alpha vocabulary), which the movement-
  denial closure (DEC-082.A R2) warns against. Presented, not recommended.
  [EC: designer ruling — DEC-082.A R2, DEC-138; recommendation]

### (c) Evidence classes & open questions

- Mechanical facts: band model from DEC-133(2); reaction machinery DEC-132.
- No empirical data (mirror-match playtest had no ZoC/pass-through scenario —
  [EC: empirical finding]).
- Open: permissive vs restrictive posture (Q4); whether entry-into-Engagement
  should also be tag-gated (recommendation: no — entry is the defender-friendly
  act; denial targets exit/passage); interplay with Seize/Deny Ground (§11).

## 7. M3 — Chase

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option K1 — sequential S-1 movement contests, band-driven)

> **Chase.** When one party (the FLEEER) moves with the declared intent to
> break off and the other (the PURSUER) declares pursuit as that turn's
> substantive action (DEC-095 — one S-1 exchange per turn), resolve a Chase as
> a sequence of S-1 opposed movement contests, one per turn, until a terminal
> condition is met:
>
> 1. **Contest each turn.** Both parties roll full Core Tests (DEC-006) on
>    declared movement-relevant Skills (DEC-025/DEC-106; e.g., an
>    athletics/evasion/pursuit-lineage Skill). Innate Movement Speed is NOT a
>    roll engine: it caps change, it does not resolve contests (§3.2).
> 2. **Band change from Quality.** The winner's Quality (DEC-031/DEC-107)
>    moves the gap one band step per content boundary (band↔hex mapping per
>    DEC-133.A R1/DEC-077.A). With the hex model (DEC-133), the winner closes
>    (or opens) the gap by their Quality in hexes, capped by effective
>    Movement Speed difference rules (below).
> 3. **Movement Speed caps closing.** A pursuer may close at most their
>    Effective Movement Speed in hexes per turn; a fleeer may open at most
>    theirs. When both have equal effective MS, the contest's Quality is the
>    only gap-changer; the Speed cap prevents runaway catches/escapes from
>    raw statistics. (DEC-133(3); DEC-004.)
> 4. **Terminal conditions (content per DEC-077.A):** (a) pursuer enters
>    Engagement with the fleeer → Chase ends, melee exchange applies;
>    (b) gap exceeds the pursuer's maximum closing range (content; e.g., the
>    fleeer's cumulative Quality edge plus a content threshold) → fleeer
>    escapes, Chase ends; (c) either party stops, is denied movement
>    (DEC-122 stack), or a terrain/hazard boundary (content) ends the Chase.
> 5. **Chase movement is the turn's movement.** Both parties' hexes moved
>    during the Chase consume their Movement Distance for the turn (DEC-095);
>    no additional movement remains for that turn.
> 6. **Consumption** of the contests themselves: Fork C (§4.1).
> 7. **Overtaking treatment:** if the pursuer's contest result would carry them
>    INTO the fleeer's Engagement band, the Chase resolves into melee per
>    rules as normal (Entry into Engagement is permitted, §6 Z1); the pursuer
>    has won condition (a).

Rationale: every roll is a full Core Test (Invariants 6/18; no no-roll engine);
Speed remains mechanically meaningful as the cap, not the resolver; one
substantive exchange per turn retained (DEC-095); relation from Quality to
geography is explicit and content-mapped. [EC: designer rulings + mechanical
facts cited; recommendation — this shape]

### (b) Alternative framings

- **Option K2 — Extended Test chase (DEC-067/068 machinery):** the Chase is one
  Extended Test (target set by GM per DEC-070), each participant rolling
  cumulative progress. Preserves Core Test economics, adds completion-target
  abstraction; loses per-turn band interplay. Register support: DEC-067/068 are
  non-canonical Extended Test proposals; the S-1/Extended relationship in the
  locked frame is the S-1-adjacent primitive. Presented as a legitimate second
  shape; choosing between K1 and K2 needs Tiwa (Q6). [EC: designer ruling —
  DEC-013 vs Extended primitives advisory; recommendation]
- **Option K3 — single decisive contest:** one S-1 roll decides catch/escape,
  Quality sets the band delta. Cheapest; no pursuit texture; recommended only
  for expedition-scale (non-tactical) play where per-turn chases are rare.
  [EC: recommendation]
- **Option K4 — Speed-vs-Speed deterministic (EXCLUDED):** comparing Movement
  Speed values with no roll is architecturally forbidden: no Core Test →
  no Cost/Overflow/XP/Double/Recovery material (Invariant 6/18; DEC-006;
  proposals-§1 identity). Deterministic comparison may only cap the rolling
  result (rule 3), never replace it. [EC: mechanical fact (Invariant 6/18),
  recommendation (the exclusion inference)]

### (c) Evidence classes & open questions

- No empirical chase data (mirror-match playtest had no chase scenario;
  replication F-05: the 45.30% Repeat rate finding warrants a follow-up before
  chase pacing is tuned — [EC: empirical finding]).
- Open: K1 vs K2 shape (Q6); terminal-condition thresholds (content);
  whether pursuer/fleeer may also attack while chasing (recommendation: No —
  one substantive action per turn, DEC-095; attack = the exchange, not the
  chase-contest; the chase itself is the exchange).

> a named mechanic (Disengage §5, ZoC §6, Chase §7, Forced Movement §9,

## 9. M5 — Forced Movement magnitude

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option F1 — Tier-scaled hexes)

> **Forced Movement (Position-tier Effect, DEC-023.A).** Upon winning a contest
> and selecting this Effect, the victor displaces the target in a declared
> direction (DEC-025):
>
> - **Magnitude:** the target moves **Y hexes**, where **Y = the Effect's
>   Tier** = the causing Skill's Skill-Tier (DEC-107), in the declared
>   direction. Band reading: content-mapped per DEC-133.A R1 (e.g., Y hexes =
>   1 band, or 1 band per Y, at content's option).
> - **Path legality:** the displacement must not pass through occupied hexes or
>   prohibited boundaries (terrain/hazard per content, DEC-077.A). Displacement
>   stops at the first obstruction; the target is not impaled or chain-shoved
>   by default (chain reactions = content, Q12).
> - **Mitigation:** the target may attempt Active Defense per the standard
>   defense machinery (DEC-050/097/103 shape): a successful AD shreds initial
>   magnitude and reduces the remainder by the AD Margin (DEC-103 step-1/step-2
>   pattern); displacement = `max(0, Y − AD_shred − AD_Margin)` hexes. A failed
>   AD provides no mitigation (DEC-097). This keeps the magnitude reading
>   record-native and defense-interactive without touching the Wound channel
>   (HP never changes from displacement itself; Impact/knock damage is a
>   separate Effect selection per DEC-024).
> - **Record form:** consistent with DEC-115/117, the outcome may be recorded
>   as `Tier-Y Forced Movement, Magnitude −Y` for bookkeeping; the spatial
>   payload is hexes moved, not a penalty to any attribute. (The Z = −Y
>   convention names magnitude; displacement is the spatial payload — the
>   DEC-115 form is reused as a recording convention, see open Q11.)
> - **Denied targets:** a target whose Effective MS is 0 (DEC-122 stack:
>   Restrained/Grappled/Stunned/Incapacitated) has no movement of their own,
>   but is still a physical body: displacement applies unless a specific
>   Condition rule forbids it (content question, Q12). Grappled-pair
>   displacement is a separate open interaction (Q12; DEC-131 covers
>   move-away, not third-party displacement).

Rationale: magnitude from the already-ruled record Tier (DEC-107/115) gives
predictable scaling with zero new economy; AD mitigation reuses the ruled
defense channel; no Quality-as-magnitude (DEC-107 preserved); no Invariant-6/
17 surface. [EC: designer rulings; recommendation — F1]

- **Option F2 — Quality/Margin-scaled displacement:** target moves the

  chosen (Q11). [EC: designer ruling — DEC-107; recommendation — prefer F1]
- **Option F3 — G1-table displacement (content table):** displacement read
  from a content-authored table (e.g., Quality band → hexes). The G1/G3 brief's

- **Option F4 — contest-delta (winner margin − loser margin) as hexes** (the

  F2. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-103/104 (wound channel); recommendation]

### (c) Open questions

- Q11: F1 (Tier-scaled) vs F2/F4 (margin-scaled) — the magnitude source fork;
  and the "record form vs spatial payload" terminology question.
- Q12: obstruction/chain-shove defaults; displacement of DEC-122-zeroed and
  Grappled targets.
- Q13: does displacement provoke its own movement-trigger reactions (e.g., a
  third party reacting to the displaced entity entering their band) — recommend
  Yes via the same tag-gated machinery, consistent with §6.

---

## 10. M6 — Pin/Hold Position resolution

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option P1 — route to existing Condition machinery)

> **Pin / Hold Position (Position-tier Effect, DEC-023.A).** Upon winning a
> contest and selecting this Effect (DEC-024/107), the victor imposes the
> existing **Restrained** Condition record on the target (DEC-079 alpha
> vocabulary; DEC-115/117 record form: `Tier-Y Restrained, Magnitude Z = −Y`,
> Location per the declared fiction / DEC-023.A(3) gating):
>
> - **Record:** `Tier-Y Restrained` where Y = the causing Skill's Skill-Tier
>   (DEC-107); Z = −Y (DEC-115). Rounds/duration per the Condition's existing
>   record rules (content of DEC-079's Restrained entry, not re-ruled here;
>   DEC-082.A R2 closure respected).
> - **Movement:** the target's Effective Movement Speed is 0 while Restrained
>   (DEC-122 overlay machinery). Action declaration remains possible but with
>   the Condition's standard denial effects (DEC-123 "never total" — the target
>   may always declare; the attempt resolves per the Condition record).
> - **Escape:** the target (or an ally with a declared intent) resolves an
>   escape attempt as a contested Break-Hold/Break-Free contest per the
>   DEC-124/131 Grappled machinery: success stepwise-removes the record (per
>   the Heal-Effect-System removal shape of DEC-131); failure = locked, no
>   relocation (DEC-131), and the attempt's cost stands (natural roll).
> - **Flavor mapping:** "Pin" = Restrained (full-body); "Hold Position" =
>   Restrained with Location-limb or a positional hold reading (Declared
>   fiction per DEC-025/023.A(3)). Both resolve through the SAME record —
>   no new Condition type is created.
> - **If the fiction is a grapple:** use the existing **Grappled** Condition
>   instead (DEC-079), with the matching move-away/break machinery (DEC-124/
>   131). Pin/Hold is the *positional* selection; Grappled is the *restraining*
>   selection; a single win picks one (DEC-024).

Rationale: maximum reuse of the ruled Condition stack (DEC-079/115/122/123/
124/125/126/131); honors DEC-082.A R2's "complete answer" closure by NOT
creating a parallel denial Condition; the record form is already the unified
pattern (DEC-115/117). [EC: designer rulings; recommendation — P1]

### (b) Alternative framings

- **Option P2 — new alpha Condition "Pinned/Held":** author a NEW Condition
  into the DEC-079 vocabulary (amendment process; alpha condition vocabulary
  currently declared "Alpha Locked" — would need an amendment ruling). More
  flavorful control (e.g., different escape DCs); cost: breaks DEC-082.A R2's
  "complete answer" reading for co-occurring denial Conditions and adds a
  fourth denial record type to maintain. [EC: designer ruling — DEC-079 alpha
  status; DEC-082.A R2; recommendation — heavier, only if Tiwa wants distinct
  Pinned mechanics]
- **Option P3 — positional-only pin (no Condition record):** pin described
  purely as geometry ("target may not leave the band while the pinner
  maintains the hold") without a Restrained record. Deceptively simple; fails
  because "may not leave the band" is movement denial that the locked stack
  expresses via the record overlay (DEC-122) — inventing a geometry-only denial
  re-opens the closed movement-denial question. [EC: designer ruling —
  DEC-082.A R2/122; recommendation]
- **Option P4 — pin as its own Effect with generated record:** same as P1 but
  with a dedicated record name routed through Condition-resolution. This is a
  labeling fork, not a mechanics fork; name choice is content (Q9).

### (c) Evidence classes & open questions

- Mechanical facts: Condition record machinery (DEC-115/117/122/131).
- No empirical evidence distinguishing P1–P4 (no hold/pin playtest).
- Open: (1) P1 vs P2 (new Condition amendment) — Q9; (2) does the pinner
  sacrifice their own movement while holding (recommendation: yes — holding
  engages the pinner's position; this is the natural reading of "Hold
  Position," but it should be stated explicitly if adopted) — Q10; (3) can
  allies carry/pull a Restrained target out of the pin (recommendation: yes,
  via the escape contest machinery, not free drag).

---

## 11. M7 — Seize/Deny Ground resolution

### (a) Candidate rules text (Option S1 — position-ownership model)

> **Seize / Deny Ground (Position-tier Effect, DEC-023.A).** Upon winning a
> contest and selecting this Effect, the victor declares a ground claim:
>
> - **Seize:** the victor declares a band/hex area (hostile Occupancy declared
>   per DEC-025). The target is displaced out of that area by **Y hexes**
>   (same Tier-scaled magnitude as Forced Movement, §9 — one convention for
>   positional payloads), and the victor occupies it. The loser may not re-enter
>   or pass through the seized area without winning a new contest (an M4
>   generic movement contest, or the §6 ZoC machinery if a movement-trigger Tag
>   applies — both are S-1, repeated attempts allowed with natural-roll costs
>   each time).
> - **Deny:** the victor declares the same area, but the *payload is a
>   prohibition*: the target may not enter/pass through while the claim
>   stands; entering is contested (as above). Deny is Seize with the
>   displacement step omitted — one resolution, two declared intents.
> - **Binary outcomes only (DEC-030):** no graded claims; a single win either
>   establishes the claimed position or does not. Duration is open to content
>   (until contested, until the victor leaves, or a content-set term — Q14).
> - **Interplay:** no double-dipping — Seize/Deny and Forced Movement are
>   separate Effect selections (DEC-024); a win that Seizes has already spent
>   its Effect slot and does not also displace via Forced Movement rules.
> - **Consumption:** Fork C (§4.1).

Rationale: gives "ground" a real positional footprint (ownership + re-entry
contest) without inventing new denial mechanics; reuses the Tier-scaled hex
convention (§9) for consistency; strictly binary (DEC-030); interacts cleanly
with ZoC (§6) as the tag-gated enforcement layer. [EC: designer rulings;
recommendation — S1]

### (b) Alternative framings

- **Option S2 — relocation-only:** Seize merely displaces the target one band
  (no persistent ownership). Simpler; loses the "seized" identity — nothing
  stops instant re-entry beyond a generic contest. [EC: recommendation]
- **Option S3 — fold into Open/Close Lane:** read Seize/Deny Ground as the
  band-general form and Open/Close Lane (DEC-023.A's positional sibling) as
  the directional form, sharing §11's resolution. Recommended as a
  consolidation to propose to Tiwa (Q15) — not silently merged here.
  [EC: recommendation]
- **Option S4 — hex-claim economy:** claims as persistent "ground tokens" that
  accumulate; explicitly NOT recommended — persistent position-tokens would
  drift into a stored economy (Invariant 17 watch) and violate the ephemerality
  principle of the movement frame. [EC: recommendation; Invariant 17 caution]

### (c) Open questions

- Q14: claim duration (until re-contested vs content-set).
- Q15: S1 vs S3 (fold with Open/Close Lane) and the Open/Close Lane mechanics
  themselves (also Position-tier alpha, also unruled — same candidate shape
  applies: directional band claim + re-entry contest).
- Q16: can the loser pass through a denied area with a successful *non-*
  movement action (e.g., teleport/transport effects)? Recommend: content per
  DEC-077.A; not framework-ruled here.

---

## 13. Invariant 6 / 17 audit (per mechanic)

| Mechanic | Invariant 6 (Cost = natural roll) | Invariant 17 (no competing economy) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Disengage | ✅ every roll is a full S-1 Core Test | ✅ no stored resources; Fork C options are ephemeral per-turn budget | Tag-gated reactions, one contest per attempt |
| M2 ZoC | ✅ same | ✅ no counters/tokens; Z4 variant flagged as penalty-overlay drift | Permissive default recommended |
| M3 Chase | ✅ K1/K2/K3 all Core Test-shaped; **K4 (Speed-vs-Speed, no roll) fails Invariant 6/18 — excluded** | ✅ contests cost natural rolls only; no chase-meter economy | Speed caps, never resolves |
